item.content:encoded:
Call it a product of injuries or just a slump, but the Red Sox are staggering into the final week of the regular season offensively.
They have averaged 2.82 runs over the last 11 games, hitting .210 with a .621 OPS.
Wilyer Abreu (7 for 36), Mickey Gasper (4 for 25), Jahmai Jones (2 for 18), Isiah Kiner-Falefa (1 for 20), Adley Rutschman (6 for 30), and Nick Sogard (8 for 40) have all gone cold.
Roman Anthony was 5 for 13 with two doubles and a home run over the weekend against the Rays after hitting .137 in his 12 prior games.
The Sox are eighth in the American League in runs scored (678, 4.35 per game). They were third last season at 4.85.
“Just got to stay with it,” interim manager Chad Tracy said after a 5-1 loss against the Rays on Sunday. “Obviously we’ve got to hit and score runs. But we’re getting our way back to health, and we’ll get there.”
The return of two of the team’s top hitters, Willson Contreras and Ceddanne Rafaela, should help.
Contreras has played only four games this month because of a strained left hamstring and a bruised right hand. He started swinging a bat Sunday and hopes to return this week after missing the Rays series.
“It’s getting better every day,” Contreras said Sunday. “We’ll see.”
Contreras leads the team in home runs (27), RBIs (81), and OPS (.905).
Rafaela should be back in the lineup Tuesday after missing 16 games with a right quadriceps strain. He has hit .282 with a .760 OPS, 16 homers, and 70 RBIs.
Caleb Durbin has reached base in 13 consecutive games, raising his on-base percentage from .324 to .338.
Trevor Story has been another positive, hitting .338 with an .869 OPS and 10 RBIs over 19 games since returning from the injured list.
Tests this week
The postseason doesn’t start until Sept. 29, but the Red Sox will get a taste of what’s to come this week at Fenway Park.
They start a three-game series against the Guardians on Tuesday before the Cubs arrive Friday.
The 81-75 Guardians hold a one-game lead over the White Sox in the American League Central. The 87-69 Cubs are tied with the Padres atop the National League wild-card race.
The Guardians have All-Star lefthander Parker Messick (12-9, 2.57) starting Tuesday with Foster Griffin (15-5, 3.67) on Wednesday. Messick faced the Sox in Cleveland on May 30 and allowed one run over five innings.
The Sox have Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez lined up in the series, which could be how they approach the Wild Card Series next week.
Honor for Arias
Shortstop Franklin Arias was named the Eastern League’s Most Valuable Player and Top Prospect by Minor League Baseball. The 20-year-old from Venezuela hit .318 with a .993 OPS in 75 games for Portland before he was promoted to Triple-A Worcester. Sea Dogs first baseman Brooks Bannon also was named to the Eastern All-Star team. The Pitcher of the Year was righthander Anthony Eyanson, who was 4-0 with a 1.69 ERA in 11 games for Portland before going to the Orioles organization in the trade for Rutschman . . . The Sox finished 46-35 on the road, a five-game improvement on last season . . . Assistant general managers Mike Groopman and Taylor Smith interviewed with the Athletics, who are searching for a head of baseball operations after firing David Forst in August. Longtime assistant GM Billy Owens also is a candidate, along with former Nationals GM Mike Rizzo and former Astros GM James Click, who now works for the Blue Jays.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Clinching celebration solidified need for Red Sox-Payton Tolle contract extension
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: The Boston Red Sox's Wild Card clinching ceremony included the usual champagne showers and dripping-wet interviews. Everyone had their moments between the clubhouse party and the team photo, but the expected star of the celebration did not disappont. Payton Tolle gave Red Sox fans everything they wanted and more out of their playoff-making party. The towering lefty is usually the most hilarious member of the Red Sox, but his antics were turned up to 11 in the presence of more beer than anyone ca
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox's Wild Card clinching ceremony included the usual champagne showers and dripping-wet interviews. Everyone had their moments between the clubhouse party and the team photo, but the expected star of the celebration did not disappont.
Payton Tolle gave Red Sox fans everything they wanted and more out of their playoff-making party. The towering lefty is usually the most hilarious member of the Red Sox, but his antics were turned up to 11 in the presence of more beer than anyone can drink.
Tolle smashed some beers Stone Cold style, danced like no one was watching and gave an under-the-influence interview fans won't soon forget. The best part is that he would probably do many of the same things sober as a judge.
Tolle has grown in to a Red Sox fan favorite in record time. His off-the-field shenanigans match up to the skill he brings on the mound. After his first season-plus with Boston, it should be doing everything in its power to keep Tolle on the team for as long as possible.
Payton Tolle's Wild Card celebration showed just how badly the Red Sox need to extend him
The Red Sox have adopted an early contract extension strategy with many of its young players, including Ceddanne Rafaela, Brayan Bello and Roman Anthony, among others. Alex Speier of The Boston Globe reported on August 18 that Boston hadn't approached Tolle about an extension at the time (subscription required). The Sox have signed so many young players that they could be taking a break, but they should re-start negotiations again for Tolle.
Not only is the 23-year-old an electric personality, he's a force on the mound. The American League's 2026 rookie class is packed to the brim with talent including Kevin McGonigle (the certain winner), Parker Messick and Munetaka Murakami, but Tolle has performed well enough to deserve a mention near the top of this year's list.
Tolle has posted a 3.02 ERA, 1.07 WHIP, 166 strikeouts and 38 walks over 143 innings. The rookie has deepened and sharpened his arsenal this season, his extension (a metric Craig Breslow loves) is elite at a staggering seven-foot-four, his 36.5 percent chase rate sits in the 96th percentile and his 28.9 strikeout percentage ranks near the top of the league. Tolle is an imposing presence on the mound with the prime of his career still years away and the Red Sox should hold onto him for as long as possible.
Tolle will most likely get a start during Boston's Wild Card series, possibly in Game 1. The Red Sox clearly trust him in big moments, he's got personality to share and he's already active in the community — he is the ideal candidate for an early contract extension.

item.title: [mlb.com] Postseason FAQ: What's next for the Red Sox?
item.dc:creator: Ian Browne

item.content:encoded:
Now, they have six regular-season games left to prepare for what is to come.
One big objective will be to get postseason baseball back to Fenway Park for the first time since 2021. After losing in three games in the 2025 AL Wild Card Series to the Yankees at Yankee Stadium, the ending felt too abrupt.
It has already been an improbable turnaround for the Red Sox, surging from 14 games under .500 on June 25 and getting to the postseason. There is a belief within the clubhouse that more magic can happen.
“I think we can make a run,” said rookie lefty Payton Tolle. “I think we’ve got the guys. I think we can get hot. We’re just going to continue to play the way that we play. That team baseball we’ve been playing. You play to get to the postseason and to give yourself a shot to go to the World Series.”
Without further ado, here are some key talking points heading into the playoffs.
What could the postseason roster look like?
C: Adley Rutschman, Connor Wong
1B: Willson Contreras
2B: Nick Sogard
SS: Trevor Story
3B: Caleb Durbin
UTIL: Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Mickey Gasper
OF: Jarren Duran, Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, Braiden Ward
DH: Roman Anthony, Jahmai Jones
SP: Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle
Bullpen: Aroldis Chapman, Garrett Whitlock, Tyron Guerrero, Erik Miller, Greg Weissert, Brayan Bello, Jake Bennett, Garrett Crochet, Tanner Houck
The most intriguing decision for the position-player roster surrounds whether to add Ward, who set the Triple-A Worcester record with 61 stolen bases this season, as a pinch-running specialist. Dave Roberts, anyone?
The bullpen situation also bears watching. Considering that Crochet hasn’t pitched since April 25 and Houck’s next appearance will be his first in the Majors since 2025, the club will monitor how both rehabbers are throwing before finalizing the roster. This could influence if the club carries Bennett as a reliever. Jovani Morán is another option from the left side.
When does the postseason begin?
For the Red Sox, the fun starts on Sept. 29, when interim manager Chad Tracy’s club participates in an AL Wild Card Series, with all games in the best-of-three series to be played on the road. The Yankees, unless they improbably take the AL East from the Rays, will be the Red Sox opponent in what will be yet another chapter in the richest rivalry in baseball. The only other scenario that can stave off another rivalry match would be the Red Sox slipping to the No. 6 seed. They lead the current No. 6 seed, the White Sox, by four games.
How have the Red Sox performed against the Yankees this season?
Last year, Boston’s hopes of getting a playoff game at Fenway Park for the first time since ‘21 ended when the team lost Game 3 of the Wild Card Series to … the Yankees in the Bronx. So, yes, this would be a rematch between the rivals. In a form befitting the rivalry, the regular-season series swayed back and forth, with New York ultimately taking seven of the 13 head-to-head encounters.
The Yankees swept the Red Sox at Fenway from April 21-23 in what wound up being Alex Cora’s last home series managing Boston. Fast forward to the Bronx from June 5-7, and the sides split, with the middle game getting postponed due to rain. For the Red Sox, their entire season started to turn around with a four-game sweep at Fenway from June 25-28. And for the Yankees, home field for this potential series was essentially wrapped up when they took three out of four from the Sox at the end of August to clinch the season series.
Will Aaron Judge be active for the Wild Card Series?
Judge’s potential participation in the series will be a huge focal point. The Yankees’ captain, limited to 66 games this season, was recently placed on the injured list again with a right calf strain. Though the Yankees have played more games without Judge than with him, his absence could make a difference for Boston.
What happens in the unlikely scenario the Red Sox slip from the No. 5 seed to the No. 6 spot?
In that case, the Red Sox would play the division champion with the worst record, which at this point would be whoever emerges victorious in a shaky AL West.
Which health situations should be monitored as the regular season winds down?
Where to start? There are many to choose from.
Contreras suffered a badly bruised knuckle between his right ring finger and pinkie when he was hit by a pitch on Sept. 17. He admitted he will be out for “days,” but hopes to be back before the postseason. It was a good sign that Contreras was able to grip a bat and take some swings on Sunday.
All eyes will be on Crochet to see if it’s possible to activate him for the playoffs as a reliever even though he hasn’t pitched since April 25 due to left shoulder inflammation.
Rafaela, the Red Sox's All-Star center fielder, has been out since Sept. 3 with a right quadriceps strain but should return before the regular season ends.
How does the rotation line up for the Red Sox?
If not for the near season-long loss of Crochet to this point, the Game 1 starter wouldn’t be in question. Tracy reordered his rotation for the upcoming series, going with Tolle on Tuesday against the Guardians, followed by Gray on Wednesday and Suarez on Thursday. Could this be the same order the Sox open the playoffs with? Tracy isn’t ready to reveal those plans yet.
How much postseason experience does Boston’s projected roster have?
Contreras and Chapman both won World Series rings while playing for the 2016 Cubs. Chapman added another one with the Rangers in ‘23. Kiner-Falefa was with Toronto last season, meaning he got to play in the epic Dodgers-Blue Jays World Series, losing one of the most dramatic Game 7s ever.
Rutschman played in five postseason games during his time with the Orioles, but none beyond the Division Series. Several players in Boston’s young core got their first taste of postseason experience last year in Abreu, Rafaela and Duran. Durbin went to the NLCS with the Brewers in ‘25. Houck and Whitlock are the only players remaining on the Boston team that came two wins from making the World Series in ‘21. Veteran shortstop Story had a solid Wild Card Series in the Bronx last year.
Suarez (4-1, 1.48 ERA in 11 outings, eight starts) had his share of October moments in Philadelphia, and Gray has a 3.26 ERA in six career playoff starts.

item.title: [nesn.com] Red Sox Final-Week Breakdown: Schedule, Playoff Stakes and Biggest Questions | NESN
item.dc:creator: Rodney Knuppel
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are headed back to the postseason, but their work is not finished. Boston enters the final week of the regular season at 84-72 after Sunday’s 5-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays. The Red Sox secured their second consecutive postseason appearance when other results around the American League eliminated the remaining path for them to fall out of the playoff field. The final six games will determine how prepared Boston looks when October begins. All six will be played at Fenway Park.
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are headed back to the postseason, but their work is not finished. Boston enters the final week of the regular season at 84-72 after Sunday’s 5-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays. The Red Sox secured their second consecutive postseason appearance when other results around the American League eliminated the remaining path for them to fall out of the playoff field.
The final six games will determine how prepared Boston looks when October begins. All six will be played at Fenway Park.
The Red Sox host the Cleveland Guardians at 6:45 p.m. ET on Tuesday, 7:10 p.m. Wednesday and 6:45 p.m. Thursday. Boston will conclude the regular season with three games against the Chicago Cubs from Friday through Sunday. Cleveland arrives with its own postseason urgency. The Guardians are attempting to protect their position from the Chicago White Sox, who remain close behind in the standings.
The Cubs enter the week at 87-69 after defeating the Cincinnati Reds 9-1. Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run Sunday and has emerged as one of the most dangerous power-speed players in the National League.
Trying To Get Right With The Bats
Boston’s most immediate assignment is restoring its offense. The Red Sox managed only six hits during Sunday’s loss to Tampa Bay. Trevor Story prevented a shutout with a ninth-inning home run, but Boston wasted its best opportunity after loading the bases in the fifth inning.
Roman Anthony struck out to end that threat. Patrick Sandoval allowed five runs, although he recovered from a four-run first inning to complete seven frames. The loss dropped Boston to 84-72.
Chad Tracy must use the final week to balance two priorities.
The Red Sox need enough intensity to sharpen their offense and settle any remaining pitching questions. They also cannot afford to exhaust or injure important players immediately before the postseason.
Bullpen Questions
The bullpen hierarchy is another issue. Close games against Cleveland and Chicago can function as postseason rehearsals, allowing Tracy to test his preferred late-inning combinations before every decision becomes potentially season-ending.
The Red Sox cannot catch Tampa Bay in the American League East, and the New York Yankees remain ahead of Boston in second place. That makes the final six games less about chasing a division championship and more about playoff positioning, health and momentum.
Boston already possesses its October invitation. The final week will determine what kind of team arrives.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox secured a spot in the postseason on Sunday, but the real work is only beginning.
The Red Sox have a date with the New York Yankees in a best-of-three Wild Card series in a couple of weeks. That will be the first team standing between the Red Sox and a trip to the fall classic. If they win that series, they will play another American League East team, the Tampa Bay Rays.
If they can beat those teams, they will have to play the Cleveland Guardians, Chicago White Sox, Texas Rangers or Houston Astros.
The path to the World series is loaded with taolent, but so are the Red Sox. They are on the side of the bracket that features the three best records in the American League. They know they have their work cut out for them, but they are confident. Breakout pitcher Payton Tolle, who could start Game 1 against the Yankees, thinks the team has everything it needs to go deep into October.
"I think we could make a run," said Tolle, per The Athletic's Jen McCaffrey. "I think we got the guys. I think we can get hot. We're just going to continue to play the way that we play. That team baseball we've been having. I'm really just excited to be in this moment again with these guys."
The Red Sox have enough stars to compete with anyone. Roman Anthony is back and healthy. How he performs in October could dictate how far the Red Sox go. On the pitching side of things, Tolle, Sonny Gray and Ranger Suárez will be asked to carry the load. They could have Garrett Crochet back as a reliever as well.
More MLB: Craig Breslow Reflects On Firing Alex Cora After Red Sox Clinch Postseason Berth

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Craig Breslow Reflects On Firing Alex Cora After Red Sox Clinch Postseason Berth

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox secured their spot in the postseason thanks to an Atlanta Braves win over the Houston Astros.
Things are going well now, but Red Sox fans remember the 10-17 start that led to Alex Cora and six other coaches being fired. Since then, interim manager Chad Tracy has led the charge in turning things around, but it has not all been him. The players started living up to expectations, and the team has gotten healthy.
At the time, many questioned Craig Breslow's ability to make decisions, with many fans saying Cora was fired as a result of Breslow failing to address the team's biggest flaws in the offseason. However, now it looks like Breslow was right to trust his players.
"I believed in the players that we had,” Breslow said when asked about the move to fire Cora, per The Athletic's Jen McCaffrey. “I felt it was really important that we acted definitively and decisively when we did so that we could create an environment around the players that was supportive, that would allow them to thrive. And they responded. While there may have been some people that questioned what this group was capable of, I think they answered resoundingly.”
One example of Breslow's belief paying off is Caleb Durbin. Durbin was acquired to replace Alex Bregman, and he was a terrible hitter through two months. However, after back-to-back off days in May, he has been on another level. He is looking more like the Rookie of the Year finalist he was for the Milwaukee Brewers last year. He looks like a real player the Red Sox can rely on down the line.
Perhaps what's most impressive about this Red Sox team is that they have turned the season around without arguably their two best pitchers, Garrett Crochet and Roman Anthony. However, Anthony is back, and Crochet could be in the bullpen for October.

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox avanza a playoffs
Roman Anthony: "Nos mantuvimos con vida cuando nadie creía que podríamos. Y aquí estamos"
Boston es el cuarto equipo en clasificar a los playoffs tras haber tenido un récord de 14 o más juegos por debajo de .500 en una temporada en la era de la Serie Mundial, desde 1903
ST. PETERSBURG, Florida.- . "Nos mantuvimos con vida cuando nadie creía que podríamos. Y aquí estamos", dijo Roman Anthony en medio de la celebración de los Medias Rojas de Boston, por su pase a la postemporada.
Mientras los Boston Red Sox celebraban su improbable clasificación a la postemporada en el Tropicana Field, con champán y cerveza a raudales, la música del vestuario parecía la más apropiada.
"Stayin' Alive".
"Creo que eso lo dice todo", declaró el jardinero izquierdo Roman Anthony el domingo, de acuerdo a un reporte de ESPN.
El 24 de junio, los Red Sox tenían un récord de 32-46 y estaban a 15 juegos y medio del liderato de la División Este de la Liga Americana. Desde entonces, han logrado un récord de 52-25 y se clasificarán para los playoffs.
Los Red Sox perdieron 5-1 contra los Tampa Bay Rays en el último partido de su serie, por lo que no pudieron asegurar su pase. Sin embargo, aproximadamente una hora después de que terminara el partido, los Houston Astros perdieron 4-2 contra los Atlanta Braves, lo que permitió a los Red Sox asegurar su lugar como comodín.
Poco después de que se confirmara el resultado del partido Astros-Braves, los jugadores, entrenadores y personal de los Red Sox se reunieron cerca del montículo del Tropicana Field para una foto de equipo.
"Realmente no me importa cómo entramos, lo importante es que entramos", dijo el campocorto Trevor Story.
Los Red Sox son el cuarto equipo en clasificar a los playoffs tras haber tenido un récord de 14 o más juegos por debajo de .500 en una temporada en la era de la Serie Mundial (desde 1903). Dos de los tres casos anteriores llegaron a la Serie Mundial, con los Boston Braves ganándola en 1914.
El manager interino Chad Tracy estuvo al mando durante gran parte de la remontada de este año. Desde su nombramiento el 26 de abril tras el despido de Alex Cora, los Red Sox tienen un récord de 74-55.
"Miren, no estábamos en una buena situación", dijo Tracy. "No estábamos jugando bien. Pero esto demuestra que si uno persevera, pueden suceder cosas buenas. No podría estar más orgulloso de este grupo".
El primera base Willson Contreras dijo que mantuvo la fe, incluso cuando las cosas iban mal, y la recompensa fue dulce.
“Es difícil no emocionarse hasta las lágrimas”, dijo Contreras. “Es un gran logro, pero no quiero que este equipo se detenga aquí. Quiero seguir adelante. Hemos demostrado que se puede estar en racha y superar grandes obstáculos”.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Red Sox Roman Anthony Makes Personal Admission After Playoff Clinch

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox lost to the Rays 5-1 on Sunday afternoon at Tropicana Field. The game itself did not matter. What happened later did.
The Braves beat the Astros to eliminate Houston from wild card contention, and the Red Sox' postseason berth became official. Players pulled on celebration gear and goggles, posed for a team photo on the field, and returned to a locker room that erupted in champagne and beer.
For one player in particular, the moment carried weight that went beyond the standings.
Anthony Gets His Moment
Roman Anthony was on the roster for last year's Wild Card Series against the Yankees. He never got to play in it. An injury kept him off the field for the biggest games of the season, and he could only watch as Boston's run ended in three games.
This year brought another injury. Anthony missed significant time before fighting his way back in August. When the celebration started Sunday, he was in the middle of it.
"I felt this a little bit last year but obviously being injured, I am so happy to be part of it now," Anthony said. "It's just an amazing feeling. Obviously, we wanted to win, but the way it happened, being together watching that game, it was amazing."
The emotion was real. Anthony has dealt with two straight seasons of injury setbacks during the most important stretches. Getting to celebrate with his teammates, healthy and contributing, meant something different for him than it did for most of the room.
Tolle Reflects on How Far The Red Sox Have Come
Payton Tolle was one of the last players to speak with reporters after the celebration had settled. His perspective captured what the locker room was feeling.
"I think it was just relief," Tolle said. "I think there's also just that feeling of like, 'Man, we've come a long way.' You know, we're going to enjoy this and be proud of it. It was a whole lot of fun."
"Obviously, you want to win, but being in is the most important thing," Tolle added.
The big left-hander has been one of the best stories of Boston's season.
Tracy and Contreras Address the Room
Chad Tracy took in the scene from the side of the room before addressing what his team had accomplished.
"At the beginning, we had a long way to go," Tracy said. "It's like, 'How do we get on track and get things moving in the right direction?' When the end of June hit and things started to go, and we started to see things come together, it became very much on our mind. So I'm just really happy for our guys."
"They stared almost an impossible task right in the face, and they refused to take no for an answer," Tracy said. "They're very battle tested, and I'm super, super proud of them."
Willson Contreras called for silence and delivered a message to his teammates.
"We create a good family here, good chemistry throughout the season," Contreras said. "We just needed time, and the time came for us. And what's the most important thing to me is that everybody never stopped working. Everybody was finding a way to make adjustments and play the game the right way."
"This is what we play for," Contreras said. "This is why we're here."
The room answered with a roar, and the celebration picked back up.
Final Word for the Red Sox
The Red Sox were 32-46 on June 24. They are in the playoffs with six games to spare.
The words from Sunday's locker room told the full story. Relief from Tolle. Pride from Tracy and Contreras. Gratitude from Anthony, who finally gets to experience what he missed a year ago.
This team earned every drop of champagne. What comes next starts September 29.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Red Sox Roman Anthony Makes Personal Admission After Playoff Clinch appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Craig Breslow proved the critics wrong, and deserves credit for the Red Sox clinching a playoff spot - The Boston Globe

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Craig Breslow stood in a puddle of beer in his stocking feet on Sunday, watching the team he assembled celebrate having clinched its spot in the postseason.
That’s when he realized he still had his phone in his pocket. The Red Sox chief baseball officer carefully picked his way down the hallway to put it out of harm’s way before he got even more soaked.
“Smart move,” Breslow was told.
“It might be too late,” he said, laughing.
You can always get a new phone. But how often can you enjoy the satisfaction of proving that an entire city, if not an entire industry, was wrong?
Breslow made what still remains the most stunning move of this baseball season when he fired Alex Cora and six of his coaches on April 25 after only 27 games.
He was convinced the team had potential it would not realize under Cora and needed a change.
“I believed in the players that we had, and I felt it was really important that we acted definitively and decisively when we did, so that we could create an environment around the players that was supportive, that would allow them to thrive, and they responded,” he said.
“And, while there may have been some people that questioned what this group was capable of, I think they answered.”
Some people? How about most of us?
It was not a straight line to success. The Sox were 13-16 in the first 29 games under interim manager Chad Tracy, and I wrote in late May that it was time to start rebuilding by getting a jump on the trade deadline.
With Roman Anthony and Garrett Crochet on the injured list, it seemed obvious the Sox weren’t going to contend. There were loud “sell the team” chants at Fenway Park.
Tracy’s record was 22-29 three weeks later, and even the players had started to question what was going on at Fenway Park.
“We’re not good. We’re just not a good team right now. That’s just a fact,” righthander Sonny Gray said after a 3-2 loss against the Blue Jays on June 18.
I wrote the next day that it felt inevitable the Sox would be sellers and could well finish the season with 95 losses. Some executives from other teams believed Breslow could only save his job by turning veterans into prospects.
You know what happened next. The Sox went on a season-saving 32-6 run and are now a threat to make a deep run into October. They are the first team in history to lose 44 of their first 75 games and make the playoffs.
“You stared impossible in the face with the position we were in,” Tracy told his players on Sunday.
Breslow did not see any particular series or moment as a turning point.
“I think the turnaround was the result of incremental change, incremental improvement, changes to the way that we practice, the ways that we trained, the way that we delivered information to our players, the way that we supported our players,” he said.
“So I think when you put all those things together, they compound, and then ultimately the performance on the field by way of wins and losses was the last thing to catch up.”
Breslow spent 12 seasons pitching in the majors and grew a beard with the rest of the wild bunch Red Sox of 2013. He appeared in 10 of the 16 playoff games that season and got three huge outs in the eighth inning of Game 6 in the ALCS.
His job now is giving others that opportunity. But in the end, you’re standing in the same puddle of beer with a big smile.
“The obvious difference is I didn’t have a direct impact on the outcomes of games in this role, whereas I did as a player,” Breslow said. “But I think there’s a different sense of gratification when you’re kind of part of this massive effort to identify players and bring them in and help support the coaching staff.
“It’s very different, and in some ways it’s maybe a couple of layers removed. But it’s certainly as satisfying.”
Breslow has earned that satisfaction. The job’s not over, but he had it right about this team.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

21 Sep 2026, 11:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Erik Williams)
Mike Yastrzemski capped a four-run sixth inning with a three-run homer, and the visiting Atlanta Braves clinched the National League East with a 4-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Sunday.
The Braves swept the three-game interleague series and claimed their seventh division pennant over the last nine seasons. Yastrzemski was the last of four batters to reach safely against Astros left-handed reliever Bryan King (3-6), who didn't record a single out and exited after allowing Yastrzemski's 12th homer of the season.
Jose Altuve and Yainer Diaz homered for the spiraling Astros, who will enter the final week of the regular season one game behind the Texas Rangers in the American League West.
Astros starter Hunter Brown allowed just three singles and two walks over five shutout innings. Braves starter Martin Perez navigated traffic, allowing just one run on six hits and two walks in 4 1/3 innings.
Rays 5, Red Sox 1
Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca and Chandler Simpson drove in two runs apiece during a four-run first inning, Victor Mesa Jr. homered and the Rays defeated visiting Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla.
With the win, the Rays completed their final regular-season homestand with an 8-1 record and wrapped their home schedule with a major league-best 55-26 mark.
Trevor Story homered, and Roman Anthony and Caleb Durbin each went 2-for-4 for the Red Sox, who managed just six hits while losing their second straight game.
Pirates 4, Royals 3
Rafael Flores Jr. belted a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth inning to cap Pittsburgh's three-game sweep over visiting Kansas City. With the win, the Pirates improved to 14-6 in their last 20 games.
Oneil Cruz went deep to lead off the fourth inning and Spencer Horwitz had an RBI single in the sixth for Pittsburgh. Carmen Mlodzinski earned the win after allowing two runs on three hits in three innings.
Vinnie Pasquantino had a pinch-hit two-run homer for the Royals, who have lost four in a row and seven of their past eight games.
Phillies 7, Mets 2
Cristopher Sanchez tossed 6 1/3 solid innings and earned the victory for visiting Philadelphia, which earned a much-needed win over New York.
Luis Arraez was 1-for-4 with two RBIs for the Phillies. Justin Crawford provided insurance in the eighth with a bases-clearing triple off Kodai Senga. Sanchez (18-6) gave up two runs on six hits. Philadelphia sits four games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks in the race for the final National League wild card.
Bo Bichette homered for the Mets, who dropped their home finale for the third time in four years, while Brett Baty had a pinch-hit run-scoring single in the seventh. Francisco Alvarez and A.J. Ewing each singled twice.
Cubs 9, Reds 1
Pete Crow-Armstrong tied the major league lead with his 45th home run, and David Peterson held host Cincinnati to one run on three hits in six innings in Chicago's win.
Crow-Armstrong was 3-for-5 with two RBIs, three runs, his 30th double and his 38th stolen base. He matched Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber at 45 homers, and he became the first center fielder in history with 40 home runs, 30 doubles and 30 steals in a season.
Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered for the Cubs. JJ Bleday hit a home run for the Reds, who have dropped three of four.
Cardinals 5, Nationals 3
Leo Bernal's two-run home run capped a three-run eighth inning, and St. Louis rallied for a win against visiting Washington to salvage the finale of the three-game series.
Ivan Herrera tied it 3-3 with one out when he hit his second solo homer of the day. Luis Gastelum (5-3) pitched a scoreless inning for the win. Jose Fermin had two hits for the Cardinals, who had lost four straight.
CJ Abrams homered, and Daylen Lile had a double and a single for Washington, which had won six of seven.
Mariners 2, Rockies 1
Kade Anderson threw seven scoreless innings, allowing just three hits in the longest outing of his rookie season, and visiting Seattle stayed alive in the postseason race with a win over Colorado in Denver.
Dominic Canzone had two hits and two RBIs for Seattle, which gained a game on the Texas Rangers in the AL West. Closer Andres Munoz left the game in the ninth with an apparent right arm injury.
Hunter Goodman's 39th home run of the season couldn't prevent Colorado from moving within one loss of its fourth consecutive 100-loss season.
Blue Jays 7, Rangers 2
Nathan Lukes and Charles McAdoo each had two RBIs to lead Toronto to a win over Texas in Arlington, Texas.
Kazuma Okamoto broke a 2-2 deadlock with an RBI single in the fifth and gave the Blue Jays a lead they would never relinquish as they remained three games back of the final AL wild-card spot. Spencer Arrighetti (9-9) picked up the win, allowing two runs in 2 1/3 innings during a bullpen game.
Jake Burger delivered the Rangers' lone runs on a game-tying two-run homer in the fourth. Jacob deGrom (11-10) had a shaky outing, giving up three runs with five hits in 4 1/3 innings for Texas, which maintained its one-game lead in the AL West despite the defeat.
Brewers 3, Orioles 0
Jacob Misiorowski set the tone with three shutout innings and Milwaukee blanked host Baltimore for the second game in a row to complete a three-game sweep and set a franchise record for regular-season victories.
William Contreras homered, and Cooper Pratt provided two run-scoring singles with two outs. Milwaukee is two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best record in the National League. Misiorowski's ERA dipped to 1.86.
The Orioles further damaged their fading playoff hopes, losing the first three games of the homestand to fall five games back of the Chicago White Sox for the final American League wild-card spot. Colton Cowser had two of Baltimore's four hits. Orioles starter Brandon Young (9-5) was charged with two runs in six innings.
Diamondbacks 8, Yankees 4
Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season to cap a five-run fifth and Arizona kept its slim National League wild-card chances alive with a victory over New York in Phoenix.
Geraldo Perdomo had two hits and two RBIs and five Arizona relievers limited the Yankees to three hits in 6 1/3 scoreless innings. The D-backs remained five games behind NL wild-card leaders Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four behind the Philadelphia Phillies with six to play.
Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who fell six games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East. The Yankees lead the American League with 216 homers. Lombard had two hits.
Twins 8, Angels 0
Dean Kremer allowed one hit over six innings and Alan Roden went 3-for-5 with a home run and four RBIs as Minnesota earned a split of its four-game series with Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif.
Josh Bell had three hits, a walk, two RBIs and a run while Brooks Lee also had three hits and scored three times for Minnesota, which finished with 13 hits. Kremer (4-5) allowed just a fourth-inning leadoff single to Vaughn Grissom.
Ryan Johnson (5-9) suffered the loss for Los Angeles, which finished the 2026 season with a 34-47 home record.
Guardians 1, Athletics 0
Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings to lift Cleveland past the visiting Athletics.
Williams (14-8) gave up only three hits while throwing 63 of 89 pitches for strikes. Steven Kwan had three hits and Cade Smith earned his 39th save as the Guardians swept the series and remain atop the American League Central.
A's starter Jack Perkins (3-12) gave up five hits and one run in six innings. Zack Gelof had two of the team's six hits as the Athletics suffered their sixth straight loss
Dodgers 3, Giants 1
Emmet Sheehan pitched brilliantly in long relief, Enrique Hernandez broke a seventh-inning tie with a run-scoring double and Los Angeles completed a three-game sweep of visiting San Francisco.
Tommy Edman homered for the Dodgers, who trailed 1-0 after one inning before Sheehan took over to start the second and held the Giants to just one hit with nine strikeouts over the next 5 1/3 scoreless innings.
Jung Hoo Lee and Victor Bericoto singled for the only hits for the Giants, who completed their road schedule with a 28-53 record. Sam Hentges (1-7) allowed a pair of one-out singles in the seventh before Hernandez's double for a 2-1 edge.
Padres 7, Marlins 3
Jake Cronenworth homered twice and knocked in a season-high five runs while Fernando Tatis Jr. also homered as host San Diego polished off a three-game sweep and finished 6-0 against Miami this season.
The Padres won their fifth straight game and are 13-1 in their last 14 games. Walker Buehler (9-6) worked 6 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and three runs.
Sandy Alcantara (13-11) absorbed the loss for the Marlins after permitting eight hits and four runs over six innings. Alcantara is winless in his last eight starts.
White Sox 8, Tigers 1
Chase Meidroth hit a two-run homer for Chicago and Sam Antonacci's two-run double highlighted a 2-for-4 performance as the White Sox waited through a rain delay of nearly four hours and played in wet, blustery conditions to beat Detroit.
Five pitchers held the Tigers to six hits and five walks as Detroit was limited to a single run for the third time in the series. Huascar Brazoban (6-2), reinstated prior to the game from the 15-day injured list (left lat strain), pitched for the first time since Aug. 24. He allowed a hit in one inning to get his first victory with the White Sox.
Tigers starter Troy Melton (8-5) allowed four runs in 3 2/3 innings, giving up four hits before exiting with a trainer. Detroit pitchers allowed eight walks, with White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas (1-for-2) drawing three of them. Eduardo Valencia went 3-for-4 for the Tigers, who were eliminated from postseason contention.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [firebrandal.com] The Red Sox Clinched a Playoff Spot by Losing. Chad Tracy’s Case for Permanent Manager Just Wrote Itself.
item.description: The Red Sox clinched a playoff spot on Sept. 20 by losing, 5-1, to the Rays in Tampa. Their ticket to October got punched about an hour later anyway, when the Braves beat the Astros three time zones away. Nobody in that clubhouse watched themselves get in. Rewind five months. item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox clinched a playoff spot on Sept. 20 by losing, 5-1, to the Rays in Tampa. Their ticket to October got punched about an hour later anyway, when the Braves beat the Astros three time zones away.
Nobody in that clubhouse watched themselves get in.
Rewind five months. Alex Cora got fired on a Saturday morning in April, with Boston sitting at 10-17. By June 24, the Red Sox were 15.5 games back in the AL East, with playoff odds cratered to 8.4%. That’s about as buried as a team gets in June.
Chad Tracy took over that wreckage on April 26 with zero big-league managing experience. Since then, Boston has gone 74-55 under him, a .573 winning percentage that would put most division leaders to shame. From July 27 through the end of the regular season, they played at a .609 clip, 28-18 down the stretch. They’re the first team in MLB history to lose 46 of their first 78 games and still finish above .500. Not one hot month. The roster Tracy built out of the wreckage. It’s the exact arc Central Maine tracked: a dreadful start, then a red-hot summer.
That’s the case for the permanent job. Not vibes. Receipts.
Beat writer Tyler Milliken called it one of the most improbable summers in baseball history, and he’s not exaggerating. A team that lost its manager in a firing nobody saw coming turned around and finished with the second-best road winning percentage in the American League.
This tweet nails how Saturday actually felt in that clubhouse:
Anticlimactic clinch, but to be on pace to go down as one of the worst Red Sox teams ever, then lock in, ignore the noise, and go on a generational run that led to postseason baseball…that’s both incredibly impressive and very much worth celebrating. See you in the Bronx. pic.twitter.com/ETJ7MEnHsj
— Jared Carrabis (@Jared_Carrabis) September 20, 2026
Anticlimactic, sure. You don’t draw up “clinch while getting shut down by Tampa’s bullpen” as the moment. But in a 162-game season, sometimes the celebration starts because of somebody else’s scoreboard, and you find out standing at your locker.
Plenty of the beat corps agrees on where the conversation goes next.
The Red Sox were 10-17 when Chad Tracy took over. A first time manager with no big league experience. He walked into a clubhouse of players that just lost a well-liked and respected manager.
Things weren’t fixed instantly, but they didn’t need to be. They got there in the end,… pic.twitter.com/etkqeb1PUe
— Gordo (@BOSSportsGordo) September 20, 2026
Gordo’s calling for a Manager of the Year case, and he’s not wrong to. Tracy walked into a room that had just lost a manager players actually liked, and he didn’t need some big culture-reset speech to fix it. He kept writing lineups, put Roman Anthony in the leadoff spot down the stretch, and let a talented roster figure itself out.
None of this happened by accident. firebrandal.com made the case for Tracy back in July, and it’s only gotten stronger since, even with the rotation health questions that never fully disappeared. Mickey Gasper’s hot stretch since his recall was part of the same story, a roster that kept finding useful players in June, July and August while the rest of the sport had already buried them.
Mike Mutnansky put it best: when the Red Sox fired Cora on a Saturday morning in April, nobody thought this team would sniff October. Now they’re one of 12 clubs still alive for a title. They’ll open as the No. 2 wild card, likely on the road against the Yankees, so nobody’s handing them anything in the Bronx.
Doesn’t matter how they get in. Tracy got them here. Give the guy the job.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — As the Boston Red Sox celebrated an improbable postseason berth at Tropicana Field, with Champagne and beer flowing all around, the clubhouse soundtrack seemed appropriate.
“Stayin’ Alive.’’
“I think that pretty much says it all,’’ left fielder Roman Anthony said Sunday. “We pretty much stayed alive when nobody else thought we could. Now here we are.’’
The Red Sox were 32-46 and 15 1/2 games back in the AL East race on June 24. They have since gone 52-25 and will be in the playoffs.
The Red Sox lost 5-1 to the Tampa Bay Rays in their series finale, so couldn’t take care of things themselves. But about an hour after the game finished, the Houston Astros lost 4-2 to the Atlanta Braves, allowing the Red Sox to secure a wild-card spot.
Shortly after the Astros-Braves result went final, Red Sox players, coaches and staff members gathered near the Tropicana Field mound for a team photograph.
“I really don’t care how we got in, as long as we got in,’’ shortstop Trevor Story said.
Interim manager Chad Tracy was in place for much of the turnaround. Since being appointed on April 26 following the dismissal of Alex Cora, the Red Sox have gone 74-55.
“Look, we were not in a good spot,’’ Tracy said. “We were not playing good ball. But it shows you that if you stick to it, good things can happen. I couldn’t be more proud of this group.’’
First baseman Willson Contreras said he kept the faith, even when things trended downward, and the reward was sweet.
“It’s hard not to have some tears over this,’’ Contreras said. “It’s a great accomplishment, but I don’t want this team to stop here. I want to keep going. We have proven that you can get hot and overcome a lot of big odds.’’
___

item.title: [mlb.com] Rays on precipice of AL East title after setting single-season record for wins at Trop
item.dc:creator: Adam Berry
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG -- After finishing their regular-season home schedule with yet another victory at Tropicana Field, the Rays are potentially one win away from clinching their first American League East championship since 2021. The Rays jumped out to a big lead against the Red Sox in Sunday afternoon’s series finale and rolled to a 5-1 win, their 55th of the season in their rebuilt and restored home dome. That capped an 8-1 homestand with three walk-off victories and three straight series victories
item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG -- After finishing their regular-season home schedule with yet another victory at Tropicana Field, the Rays are potentially one win away from clinching their first American League East championship since 2021.
The Rays jumped out to a big lead against the Red Sox in Sunday afternoon’s series finale and rolled to a 5-1 win, their 55th of the season in their rebuilt and restored home dome. That capped an 8-1 homestand with three walk-off victories and three straight series victories against the Astros, A’s and Red Sox, who clinched a spot in the postseason before leaving town anyway thanks to Houston’s loss to Atlanta.
“They're all big, but today was big -- and just incredibly impressed with the way the guys have gone about their business,” manager Kevin Cash said. “We knew this was going to be a big homestand, and they played extremely well.”
The Yankees’ 8-4 loss to the D-backs on Sunday afternoon extended the Rays’ division lead to six games with seven left to play. Tampa Bay only needs to win one game in the four-game series at Yankee Stadium that starts with a doubleheader on Tuesday to officially wrap up the top seed in the league.
“This month hasn't been easy by any terms. Been playing teams either in the playoffs or fighting for playoff spots. So it's been a dogfight this month,” starter Nick Martinez said. “I think we just did a good job of staying focused on what we do best and keeping our eyes ahead.”
Before flying to New York, they had to finish the home portion of their regular-season schedule on a similarly high note as they moved a season-high 35 games over .500 at 95-60.
The Rays put together a 55-26 record at the Trop this season, the third-highest home winning percentage in franchise history behind 2008 (57-24, .704) and the pandemic-shortened 2020 campaign (20-9, .690). Three of their “home” wins in ‘08 came at Disney’s Wide World of Sports, so they actually set a franchise record this season by winning 55 games at the Trop.
Tampa Bay’s players, coaches and staff knew they would appreciate being back in their longtime home ballpark this season after spending last year playing outdoors at George M. Steinbrenner Field after the Trop was damaged by Hurricane Milton. They showed it on the field all season, and they’ll get more opportunities to display their home-field advantage in the postseason.
“I think after last year, we kind of missed this place,” outfielder Jonny DeLuca said.
What has made Tropicana Field such a welcome home for these Rays? Jax pointed out that visitors typically aren’t comfortable underneath the Trop’s tilted roof, unaccustomed to the turf, the catwalks and everything else that makes this place unique.
“I think just the fact that a lot of other teams with 'natural' stadiums didn't want to play here, and us embracing that, everything that the city and the stadium just went through, and just making it our home,” left fielder Chandler Simpson added. “I feel like we're a scrappy, get-our-hands-dirty type of team, and I feel like the stadium fits that.”
Of course, the Rays have proven they can win just about anywhere when they play the kind of game they did in Sunday’s finale.
The Rays’ first three batters loaded the bases against Red Sox lefty Patrick Sandoval, then DeLuca drove in two of them with a double to left. Junior Caminero and DeLuca immediately scored on a single by Simpson, giving Tampa Bay’s pitching staff a sizable lead.
That was the first time since May 18, 2022, that the Rays’ first five batters reached consecutively to begin the game, and Victor Mesa Jr. added to their advantage in the fourth by ripping his 14th homer of the season out to right field.
“It's a bunch of good at-bats that we can string together from one to nine in our lineup, and they just continue to put pressure on pitchers,” Cash said. “Then we've got the right guys to come through in those moments.”
Jax hardly needed that kind of breathing room, as he struck out five over five scoreless innings, giving him a 0.60 ERA in three starts since Sept. 9. He ran into one jam in the fifth, loading the bases with two outs, but struck out Roman Anthony to finish another strong performance.
Next stop: New York. Next celebration: Tuesday?
“We knew what we had to do,” Jax said. “We wanted to put ourselves in a good place going into New York, make it a little bit easier.”

item.title: [Boston Herald] ‘Battle-tested’ Red Sox eager to prove they’re ready for more in postseason
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr

The achievement was dampened, and not only in the literal sense by the champagne with which the Red Sox doused each other and the room. item.content:encoded:
As the clinch celebration played out in the Tropicana Field visitors’ clubhouse early Sunday evening, the incompleteness of the moment was not lost on the revelling Boston Red Sox.
The achievement was dampened, and not only in the literal sense by the champagne with which the Red Sox doused each other and the room. That they had lost the series to the Tampa Bay Rays barely an hour earlier and instead had their ticket punched via an Atlanta Braves victory over the Houston Astros. The Red Sox are 9-9 this month, struggling offensively, without on several injured stars, and are their first postseason round will almost certainly be a rematch of last year’s best-of-three Wild Card series at Yankee Stadium, where they fell to their rivals 2-1.
In other words, there is much work to be done. The Red Sox know it, and they are eager to prove they did not come this far to only go this far.
“This has been a turbulent season,” Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow told reporters. “This is certainly an accomplishment, but it’s not the primary objective here.”
But neither the recent struggles nor the battles ahead should diminish the magnitude of the overall achievement of getting to this point.
The Red Sox lost American League Cy Young runner-up Garrett Crochet to a shoulder injury in mid-April, and he has yet to return.
They fired manager Alex Cora and several coaches in the middle of a late-April road series in Baltimore, and promoted Triple-A Worcester skipper Chad Tracy and several others from their minor league coaching ranks.
Injuries sidelined star outfielder Roman Anthony and veteran shortstop Trevor Story from early May until the very end of August.
The Red Sox owned their worst home record to start a season since 1932, and were 15 1/2 games out of first in the American League East in June.
On June 24, they fell to 14 games under .500. On Sunday, they became the fourth team in Major League Baseball history to go from as many as 14 games under .500 to the postseason in the same season.
“We needed time, and the time came for us,” veteran first baseman Willson Contreras told his teammates in the clubhouse. “I’m very proud of you all.”
“It’s 162 for a reason,” echoed third baseman Caleb Durbin.
“Obviously, getting where we want to go, but ultimately, what we had to overcome to get here makes it all the more sweet,” Tracy said. “We had a long way to go, and they never stopped, and they didn’t take no for an answer.”
This year looked lost, and the Red Sox managed to save it. They maintained an unshakeable belief in themselves, and it has already taken them to places most of the baseball world doubted it could go.
“Belief, belief, belief,” Contreras told reporters. “That was my main word, and that’s what I did from Day 1.”
The Red Sox are not a perfect team. But they certainly have the grit and gumption to go further than expected, as evidenced by the fact that they have already done so by reaching this point.
“We know how it felt when we left New York at the end of the year,” Story said. “You know how it made me feel. So that stayed with me.”
“They came together, and they found a way to get it done, and they had a long way to go to do it,” Tracy said. “They’re very battle-tested, and I’m super, super proud of them.”
“We don’t care where we play,” Tracy said. “You go back to July, and most people didn’t think we’d even be standing here. So it doesn’t matter where we play.”
“We’re in,” Tracy continued. “You got a ticket to the dance, and now you got to go take care of it there.”
“We’re in, baby,” Story said. “Let’s go.”
“Now, this is the moment,” right-fielder Wilyer Abreu said, “that we (were) waiting for.”

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Red Sox appear to be getting rotation in line for Wild Card Series - The Boston Globe
item.dc:creator: Peter Abraham
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Red Sox will start Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez in the series against the Guardians that starts Tuesday at Fenway Park. That would conceivably line them up for the Wild Card Series that starts on Sept. 29 with six days rest each. “Don’t read into that yet,” interim manager Chad Tracy said Sunday before a 5-1 loss against the Rays. “We can line that up still however we want.” True. item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Red Sox will start Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez in the series against the Guardians that starts Tuesday at Fenway Park.
That would conceivably line them up for the Wild Card Series that starts on Sept. 29 with six days rest each.
“Don’t read into that yet,” interim manager Chad Tracy said Sunday before a 5-1 loss against the Rays. “We can line that up still however we want.”
True. But Tolle has a 2.44 ERA in his last eight starts. He also has faced the Yankees twice this season and allowed one run on four hits over 13 innings with three walks and 18 strikeouts.
Gray allowed three runs on nine hits over 13⅔ innings in two starts against the Yankees. He struck out 12 and walked three.
Guerrero returns
Righthanded reliever Tyron Guerrero returned from a 19-day stint on the injured list with shoulder inflammation. Righthanded reliever Wyatt Olds was optioned to Triple-A Worcester.
Guerrero pitched a perfect eighth inning, striking out two.
“Felt good to be out there,” Guerrero said. “If I get a few more games I’ll be fine [for the postseason].”
Guerrero, 35, was called up in May for his first major league stint since 2019. He emerged as a reliable late-inning option, posting a 3.18 ERA over 39 games.
“He’s obviously a very important piece to this puzzle in our bullpen,” Tracy said.
Olds deserved a better fate. The 27-year-old has a 1.20 ERA and 1.20 WHIP in 13 games since making his major league debut on Aug. 17.
“Very tough. He’s thrown the ball great. He’s got big stuff,” Tracy said. “We had to make a roster decision.”
Contreras doing better
Willson Contreras took some swings in the batting cage to test his bruised right hand and came through fine. He said he hopes to be able to do more on Tuesday. “Step in the right direction,” Tracy said … There was no update on Garrett Crochet, who has yet to face hitters. That could come in the next few days … Tanner Houck had a 3.38 ERA over eight innings in four minor league games. Tracy suggested he would face hitters in a simulated game early this week. “Figuring out the next steps at home — and want to figure that out — but no plans for the next outing,” Tracy said. Could Houck be activated? “It’s possible,” Tracy said. “At this point, it’s going to depend very much on where’s the roster at, what are the needs, and then go from there.”… Rays shortstop Taylor Walls showed his baseball acumen in the first inning. With Roman Anthony on first and one out, he allowed Adley Rutschman’s popup to drop. Walls picked up the ball and flipped to second to get the force on Anthony. That left the Sox with a slower runner on first. It ultimately didn’t matter as Trevor Story struck out … Worcester, as Double-A Portland also did last weekend, had its final game rained out. The WooSox finished 76-67. Kutter Crawford was at Polar Park, and the plan was to have him start what would have been a bullpen game. Crawford has not appeared in a major league game since Sept. 28, 2024. He missed the 2025 season because of an injured right knee. He injured his right wrist in August of that season doing yard work at his home in Florida. Crawford pitched three innings in a rehab game for Worcester on April 11 but had a setback and wasn’t cleared for a game until Sunday. “He got to a point where he wanted to go out there and throw one,” Tracy said.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Roman Anthony headlines loaded Bowman Chrome checklist that should get Red Sox fans excited
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ranaudo
item.description: If you're not already a card collector, Red Sox fans, here's the quick version of what product sports cards enthusiasts are going crazy over right now. Bowman Chrome is Topps' flagship prospect release, the one product every year built specifically around getting a player's first-ever card into the hobby before he's played a single big-league game.
