item.content:encoded:
A brilliant pitching performance by Brayan Bello -- his best of the season -- wasn’t enough. Instead, the Rays earned a hard-fought, 2-1 victory in walk off fashion in the bottom of the ninth on Saturday at Tropicana Field.
Richie Palacios ended it with a bloop single to right against Garrett Whitlock.
Bello was the story for Boston. The righty was dominant and efficient, firing eight innings and 93 pitches while allowing five hits, walking none and tying his career high with 11 strikeouts.
It was the continuation of a strong upward trend for Bello, whose rough first two months of the season landed him back in Triple-A for five weeks.
Roman Anthony continued his solid weekend in his home state by belting an RBI double in the top of the second to break the scoreless tie and stake the Sox to a 1-0 lead.
Jonathan Aranda answered for the Rays in the fourth with an equalizing solo homer to lead off the fourth.
Neither team scored again until Tampa Bay won it in the bottom of the ninth. MVP candidate Junior Caminero caught a break when his seemingly routine foul popup hit one of the catwalks, allowing him to extend the at-bat. He made the most of it, belting a leadoff single to left. Chandler Simpson kept it going with a one-out single.
Palacios did the rest.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Red Sox waste dazzling performance by Brayan Bello, get walked off by Rays
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: Someone only tuning into their first Red Sox game of the season Saturday might not understand the significance of Brayan Bello’s dominant performance against the hosting Tampa Bay Rays. Particularly as it will be forever marred by a Rays’ 2-1 walk-off victory that keeps Boston’s postseason ticket dangling out of reach for at least another night. But before that frustrating ending, there was Bello’s hard-earned triumph. It has been a tumultuous year for the homegrown right-hander, who lost his sp
item.content:encoded:
Someone only tuning into their first Red Sox game of the season Saturday might not understand the significance of Brayan Bello’s dominant performance against the hosting Tampa Bay Rays.
Particularly as it will be forever marred by a Rays’ 2-1 walk-off victory that keeps Boston’s postseason ticket dangling out of reach for at least another night.
But before that frustrating ending, there was Bello’s hard-earned triumph. It has been a tumultuous year for the homegrown right-hander, who lost his spot in the Red Sox starting rotation at the beginning of May, and pitched his way into a Triple-A demotion the first week of June. Bello dominated in a bulk-relief role from his mid-July recall through early September before the Red Sox gave him another chance to start.
Making his second start of the month on Saturday, Bello turned in not only his best game of the season, but one of the best of his five-year career. He owned his team’s first-place division rivals for eight innings of one-run ball. He yielded just five hits, issued no walks and matched his career-high 11 strikeouts.
“That was exceptional,” Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters postgame. “By far and away his best outing of the year. As good as I’ve seen him. So, I don’t know what else to say. He was awesome, really awesome.”
Bello’s reward was a no-decision, as the Red Sox lineup went 1 for 11 with runners in scoring position, then lost on Rays second baseman Richie Palacios’ walk-off RBI single in the bottom of the ninth.
Palacios’ game-winning hit came moments after a base-running gamble by Red Sox third baseman Caleb Durbin that proved calamitous. A glimmer of hope flared when Durbin collected his second double of the day, off Bryan Baker with one out in the top of the ninth. But he was then caught trying to steal third, which proved costly almost instantaneously when Jarren Duran tripled on the very next pitch. Isiah Kiner-Falefa’s inning-ending groundout sent the tie game to the bottom of the ninth.
“I’m OK with it,” Tracy said of Durbin’s attempt to steal. “It’s one-to-one game the whole way, and close play.”
“Hindsight is 20/20,” Tracy continued. “It’s easy in baseball. He gets thrown out, and then Duran has a triple. But you don’t have the privilege of hindsight. So (Durbin) was working hard out there, seeing if he can get the bag, and they got him.”
“I thought I had a window, and probably wasn’t a big enough window,” Durbin told reporters. “I those situations, too, you want to be sure about it. So obviously on me. Not really any excuse other than I gotta be more sure.”
Roman Anthony gave the Red Sox an early lead for the second straight game, doubling off Rays starter Freddy Peralta with two outs in the third. Anthony’s third RBI base hit of the series scored Durbin, who led off the frame with his first double.
But that was all the Red Sox wrote. The home team peppered the middle innings with costly mistakes, but the visitors never took advantage.
Rays centerfielder Cedric Mullins reached safely on a bunt single and advanced to second on a throwing error by Durbin to begin the bottom of the third, but Boston’s third baseman immediately atoned for the miscue by completing a caught-stealing relay with catcher Adley Rutschman and shortstop Trevor Story.
Tampa Bay ran out of ABS challenges by the fourth inning. Shortstop Jorge Mateo burned one on a called Strike 3 from Bello (1.2” Edge Distance) for the second out of the bottom of the third. Peralta lost his team’s remaining bid trying to overturn a Ball 4 with a 2.8” Edge Distance, which put right-fielder Wilyer Abreu on with one out in the fourth.
The worm turned in the bottom of the fourth. Boston’s squandering of a one-out opportunity with Abreu and Nick Sogard (single) on first and second in the top of the inning proved costly immediately when Jonathan Aranda led off the bottom with a first-pitch, game-tying home run.
An undeterred Bello held fast to the knot inning after inning, and looked effortless doing so. Whereas Peralta exited after 5 2/3 innings that required 97 pitches (59 for strikes), Bello needed 55 pitches to complete the first five frames, and his count sat at 68 at the end of the sixth.
When the Rays finally threatened in the bottom of the seventh, the Sox starter was the picture of poise. Unruffled by the back-to-back singles by Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson, Bello retired the next three men in order. The game became his longest of the season as a starter or reliever when he recorded the first out of the seventh, and when he returned to the dugout after finishing the eighth inning, it marked his deepest outing since his complete game on July 8, 2025.
With closer Aroldis Chapman still unavailable due to lat tightness, it fell to righty Garrett Whitlock to pitch the game to extra innings. Whitlock was one strike away from stranding slugger Junior Caminero and Simpson when Palacios sent his 1-2 sinker to right field, where it plunked down in front of Abreu.
The loss means Sunday is the earliest the Red Sox can punch their ticket to October. The current playoff picture has the Red Sox and Yankees meeting in a rematch of last year’s best-of-three Wild Card series at Yankee Stadium. If Boston gets beyond that, they could see Tampa Bay again.
Saturday’s intensity felt like a preview to the Red Sox. Durbin hopes they can turn the experience into an advantage.
“That was a hell of a baseball game,” Tracy said. “I don’t have really anything negative to say about that game, other than it was really well-played on both sides by both teams. Big moments, and people rose the occasion. It was just a heck of a baseball game, and they were able to beat us.”
“Even yesterday and tomorrow, like they got a little bit of a playoff feel,” Durbin said. “I feel like last year (with the Milwaukee Brewers), first couple playoff games … adrenaline’s way higher. So to get that feel before playoffs even start is super important, because it usually takes a couple games to really settle in. So if we could settle in by Game 1 or 2, that’ll be big for us.”

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox could not have asked much more from Brayan Bello on Saturday. Unfortunately for Boston, nearly everything around him went wrong at the worst possible moments.
Bello delivered eight outstanding innings, but the Red Sox squandered several scoring opportunities before the Tampa Bay Rays walked off with a 2-1 victory at Tropicana Field. Richie Palacios ended the game with a two-out single off Garrett Whitlock, bringing Junior Caminero home from third base. The loss dropped Boston to 84-71 and evened the three-game series at one victory apiece.
Here are four takeaways from Saturday’s game:
Bello Brilliant In Tough-Luck Start
Bello did everything necessary to earn a victory. The right-hander allowed only one earned run on five hits over eight innings. He did not issue a walk, struck out 11 and threw 65 of his 93 pitches for strikes.
FINAL: Rays 2, #RedSox 1
— Red Sox (@RedSox) September 19, 2026
Bello retired the first three batters he faced and struck out seven through his first five innings. Tampa Bay’s only run against him came when Jonathan Aranda opened the fourth inning with a 361-foot home run.
The Rays threatened again in the seventh after singles from Lathan Hicks and Chandler Simpson placed two runners aboard with nobody out. Bello escaped without allowing a run, getting Víctor Mesa Jr. on a groundout, Palacios on a fielder’s choice at the plate and Cedric Mullins on a strikeout.
Bello finished the eighth by retiring Tampa Bay in order. He set down 17 of the final 20 hitters he faced and ended the afternoon with a season-high 11 strikeouts.
Boston Offense Wastes Its Chances
The Red Sox collected eight hits but finished only 1-for-11 with runners in scoring position and stranded eight runners. Boston scored its only run in the third inning. Caleb Durbin opened the frame with a double, advanced to third on Jarren Duran’s sacrifice bunt and scored when Roman Anthony doubled to center field.
That was all the Red Sox produced against Freddy Peralta and four Tampa Bay relievers.
Boston placed two runners aboard in both the fourth and sixth innings without scoring. Adley Rutschman doubled with one out in the eighth, but Wilyer Abreu struck out and Nick Sogard lined out to end the threat.
The most frustrating missed opportunity arrived in the ninth.
Durbin doubled with one out but was caught trying to steal third. Duran then tripled to center field, a hit that almost certainly would have scored Durbin had he remained at second. Isiah Kiner-Falefa grounded out to strand Duran and keep the game tied.
Ninth Inning Unravels On Whitlock
Whitlock entered for the bottom of the ninth after Bello’s terrific afternoon and immediately surrendered a single to Caminero. Whitlock retired Jonny DeLuca before Simpson added another single. A passed ball charged to Connor Wong moved both runners into scoring position, although Whitlock responded by striking out Mesa for the second out.
He could not escape the inning.
Palacios lined a 2-2 sinker into right field, allowing Caminero to score the winning run. The run was unearned because of Wong’s passed ball, but Whitlock took the loss after surrendering three hits in two-thirds of an inning.
MORE: How the Red Sox Can Clinch a Playoff Spot on Saturday
Series Finale Takes On Added Importance
Boston entered Saturday with a chance to take another significant step toward securing its postseason spot after winning Friday’s series opener. Instead, the Red Sox will need to regroup quickly following one of their most frustrating losses of the season.
The defeat dropped Boston to 84-71 and left the Red Sox 10 1/2 games behind the first-place Rays in the American League East. More importantly, it prevented Boston from building additional momentum in the wild-card race.
The Red Sox and Rays will decide the series Sunday at Tropicana Field. First pitch is scheduled for 3:10 p.m. ET.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Roman Anthony’s underwhelming return to Red Sox from injury shows unfortunate pattern
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: It felt like Roman Anthony was an instant star for the Boston Red Sox upon his call-up last season, but the truth of the matter was that it took a while for the hot-shot youngster to truly get going. item.content:encoded:
It felt like Roman Anthony was an instant star for the Boston Red Sox upon his call-up last season, but the truth of the matter was that it took a while for the hot-shot youngster to truly get going. Over his first 15 major league games, Anthony hit just .114/.291/.272.
The end result was a .292/.396/.463 performance over 71 games. We weren't complaining. It looked like the Red Sox had a perennial All-Star on their hands. Yet, thinking back on those first few games, it might have been the start of a trend.
It's not uncommon for even the best prospects to initially struggle during the first few games of their big league debut, but what has gone on since makes it seem like there's more than meets the eye.
Anthony started 2026 in a miserable slump, hitting just .229/.354/.321 before his finger ligament injury. That almost doesn't tell the whole story, though. The 22-year-old began to turn it on once the calendar flipped to May, with five hits and two walks over 15 plate appearances before landing on the IL.
The Red Sox better hope that Roman Anthony is just a slow starter and that he'll get in gear in time for October
After missing nearly four months, it was as if the youngster was starting his season again from scratch. Initially, he hit the ground running going 10-for-22 over his first five games back. But then he hit a wall. Over his last 11 games, Anthony is hitting just .149/.216/.213. His eagle eye at the plate has disappeared with just a 7.8% walk rate during that span, compared to an alarming 35.3% K-rate.
The struggles have led to calls for him to be dropped lower in the lineup. That might be a temporary solution, but even more important is that he snaps out of his funk soon.
Plenty of players throughout baseball history have gotten off to slow starts only to rebound; some have even made slow starts a habit throughout their careers. Habitually starting off behind the eight ball isn't ideal, but in the grand scheme of things, it's not catastrophic, either.
2026 saw plenty of prominent players get off to ice cold starts. Fernando Tatis Jr. didn't hit until nearly June. Old friend Alex Bregman looked washed with the Chicago Cubs before turning on the jets in the second half. Caleb Durbin no longer looks like a tragic mistake (September struggles, notwithstanding).
Given how long Anthony was on the shelf, it's almost as if he has had two Opening Days. If he truly is a chronically slow starter, that explains away the issues we're currently seeing. He's certainly not worried about it.
“I’m right where I want to be… I came back with enough time to get a good number of plate appearances, and to fail like I am right now and to succeed like I did in the beginning, and then kind of meet in the middle… [The playoffs are] what you play for after such a long year… At the end of the day, those few weeks are the only thing that really matters,” Anthony said.
It almost sounds as if Anthony was planning on this being a process, with the goal of getting back on track for the playoffs. Now, he'll have to make sure that comes to fruition; otherwise, the Red Sox will be in rough shape once the postseason rolls around.

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox enter Saturday with the opportunity to clinch a postseason berth.
In Friday’s series opener, Roman Anthony hit the longest home run of his career en route to a 4-2 victory, which snapped Tampa Bay’s six-game winning streak.
The Sox’ magic number is down to two following the win. Two scenarios would secure a postseason berth for Boston on Saturday: A Sox victory and Blue Jays victory over the Rangers, or a Sox victory, Blue Jays loss, and Braves win over the Astros.
The Sox will turn to righthander Brayan Bello, who pitched 1 ⅔ scoreless innings out of the bullpen in his last appearance against Texas on Tuesday.
Righthander Freddy Peralta will take the mound for the Rays. He faced the Sox on July 11 while a member of the Mets, allowing two runs on three hits in 4 ⅓ innings.
Here’s a preview.
RED SOX (84-70): Anthony LF, Gasper DH, Rutschman C, Wilyer Abreu RF, Sogard 1B, Story SS, Durbin 3B, Duran CF, Kiner-Falefa 2B
Pitching: RHP Brayan Bello (6-7, 4.74 ERA)
RAYS (93-60): Diaz DH, Aranda 1B, Caminero 3B, Hicks C, Simpson LF, Mesa Jr. RF, Palacios 2B, Mullins CF, Mateo SS
Pitching: RHP Freddy Peralta (9-11, 4.67 ERA)
Time: 4:10 p.m.
TV, radio: NESN, WEEI-FM 93.7
Red Sox vs. Peralta: Wilyer Abreu 0-5, Willson Contreras 7-26, Jarren Duran 3-7, Caleb Durbin 1-1, Isiah Kiner-Falefa 4-9, Andruw Monasterio 1-1, Adley Rutschman 0-3, Nick Sogard 0-2, Trevor Story 1-9, Connor Wong 1-2
Rays vs. Bello: Jonathan Aranda 6-19, Junior Caminero 1-9, Jonny DeLuca 0-2, Yandy Diaz 8-21, Jake Fraley 3-5, Nick Fortes 1-5, Liam Hicks 0-3, Richie Palacios 0-2, Jorge Mateo 2-7, Cedric Mullins 4-16, Chandler Simpson 1-3, Taylor Walls 2-17
Stat of the day: Opponents were batting .280 off Peralta’s changeup with the Mets, but they’ve hit .097 off it over the last month.
Notes: Peralta posted a 4.99 ERA in 22 starts with the Mets, but since being acquired by Tampa Bay on Aug. 2, he’s posted a 3.86 ERA in eight starts. Over his past four outings, he’s allowed just two runs on 10 hits, with 17 strikeouts and a 0.78 ERA … Willson Contreras remains day-to-day after getting hit on the right hand in Thursday night’s victory at Texas, and the Sox are confident he dodged a serious injury. Tracy said Friday he would not rule out Contreras playing this weekend …. The Sox enter Saturday 5½ games behind the Yankees for the first wild card spot. The Yankees trail Tampa Bay by 4 games for the AL East division lead.
Matty Wasserman can be reached at matty.wasserman@globe.com. Follow him @Matty_Wasserman.

item.content:encoded:
When the Boston Red Sox lost Roman Anthony to an injury in early May, little did anyone know what was about to happen. He would miss the next four months. However, while he was out, the Red Sox went on multiple winning streaks and are now closing in on a postseason berth.
Since coming back, Anthony has been slotted back into the top of the lineup by interim manager Chad Tracy. On Friday night against the Tampa Bay Rays, Anthony showed what he means to the top of the lineup.
Roman Anthony Leads Boston Red Sox To Win Over Tampa Bay Rays
Coming off a 4-3 win over the Texas Rangers, Anthony led off the game with a solo home run. In the second inning, he had a two-run single for a 3-1 lead in what turned into a 4-2 Boston victory. The win moved the Red Sox on the cusp of a postseason berth. They can clinch it as early as Saturday night.
After Anthony’s 2-for-5 night with three of Boston’s four RBIs, Tracy didn’t beat around the bush about what his young outfielder means to his club. Despite his struggles, Tracy has not moved Anthony lower in the lineup.
“You see what he can do,” Tracy said, per Peter Abraham of the Boston Globe. “It’s the game of baseball. There are ebbs and flows . . . When he’s going well, you can see the impact he makes.”
Anthony returned in late August, but his September has been a struggle. He is slashing .214/.335/.374 with four home runs and nine runs driven in this month. For Anthony, it’s all about getting ready for postseason baseball. That’s what Friday night’s game felt like.
“Obviously that’s a great team over there,” Anthony said, per Abraham. “It kind of felt like a playoff game and getting into that mode.”
Roman Anthony Credits Hitting Coach for Turning Things Around
After missing four months, it’s not easy to come back and hit MLB pitching. It doesn’t matter how many rehab assignments someone makes in the minors. Anthony has stayed the course and kept working with hitting coach John Soteropulos.
“He’s amazing. He’s somebody who knows my swing so well. We have been together since I came into this org, really, all throughout the Minor Leagues. Having somebody here, somebody who knows my swing and when to talk, nobody knows me better than John,” said Anthony, per Ian Browne of MLB.com. “I give so much credit to him in helping me out and getting into the video room and the cage and making sure everything is where we want it to be.”
Over their last 10 games, Boston is 5-5 thanks to wins over the Rangers and Rays. In 10 days, they will begin the American League wild-card series on the road, most likely in the Bronx against the New York Yankees. If Tampa Bay falters over the next week, New York could sneak up and win the division, which would send Boston to Tampa Bay for the wild-card series.
Regardless of who the Red Sox play, Roman Anthony is heating up, and that could be good news for the Red Sox and bad news for the rest of the playoff field.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — When Roman Anthony returned to the Boston Red Sox three weeks ago after nearly four months on the injury list with a torn right finger ligament, it initially looked as if he had barely missed any time.
Through his first five games after he was activated Aug. 30 in New York, Anthony recorded four games with multiple hits, going 10-for-22 with two homers, two doubles and a triple. His methodical rehab, missing 101 games, paid dividends with a bat that was ready to perform.
Advertisement
But then, as so often happens in baseball, he fell out of rhythm at the plate, collecting just seven hits, including just one extra-base hit, in his next 56 plate appearances.
That’s why he found himself in an early batting practice session Friday afternoon with hitting coach John Soteropulos, tinkering in the cage with a few mechanical adjustments.
The work clicked.
Oh baby, Roman! pic.twitter.com/aP7bBEgZX0
— Red Sox (@RedSox) September 18, 2026
Three pitches into the game, Anthony clubbed a solo homer for a lead, and in the second inning, he smacked a bases-loaded single to drive in two more runs as the Red Sox beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-2, snapping the Rays’ six-game win streak. The win inched the Red Sox closer to clinching a playoff berth. A Red Sox win Saturday, coupled with a Texas Rangers loss, would punch Boston’s ticket to the playoffs.
“We came out and looked really good offensively in the first part of that game, and there was a lot of energy in the dugout,” interim manager Chad Tracy said. “I think guys feel it. We’re not done yet, but I definitely think they sniff it, and we’re wanting to get there for sure.”
With eight games left in the regular season, getting Anthony’s bat hot again, particularly as Willson Contreras remains day to day with a deeply bruised right hand, will be imperative for the Red Sox lineup in the postseason.
“He will,” Tracy said confidently about Anthony’s bat regaining momentum. “I mean, you see what he can do. It’s the game of baseball, there’s ebbs and flows. He came off the rehab, and for like five games, he looked fantastic. Then he went through some stuff, and now he’s starting to look good again. When he’s going well, you see the impact he can make.”
Before Soteropulos was elevated to lead hitting coach this season after an overhaul of the coaching staff, he was the minor-league hitting coordinator and worked closely with Anthony. That relationship has helped.
Advertisement
“Me and John have been working on some things, really since I have been back,” Anthony said. “He’s amazing. He’s somebody who knows my swing so well. We have been together since I came into this org, all throughout the minor leagues. Having somebody here, somebody who knows my swing and when to talk and when to tinker. Nobody knows me better than John.
“It’s such a constant game of adjustments and looking over a span of my last few at-bats, it obviously was not where I wanted to be. I was hitting the ball on the ground, to the right side, so I was trying to get away from that. Hitting early on the field with John and with Trevor (Story) definitely helped.”
Anthony’s first-inning homer came off the bat at an estimated 107.7 mph with an estimated distance of 438 feet, marking the longest homer of his career.
But to him, the two-run single was just as important. In a rough series in Texas, the Red Sox had gone just 1-for-18 with runners in scoring position. His goal was to alleviate some pressure on the offense by simply making contact.
“That’s my job, to do everything I can to put the ball in play and find ways on base,” he said. “That’s how I have had a lot of success in the past as a leadoff hitter. So over these last games, just keep putting an emphasis on being the best leadoff hitter I can be. See as many pitches I can and try and get on base. It was a huge way to start the game. This game is all about momentum, so any time you can get something like that going, it’s huge.”
The two-run single gave the Red Sox the lead back after the Rays tied the score off Ranger Suarez in the bottom of the first. Jahmai Jones made it 4-1 in the third with his sixth homer of the year.
The insurance gave the Red Sox a cushion as Suarez was uncharacteristically spotty with command, walking a career-high five batters.
Advertisement
Still, he navigated traffic in each of the first four innings and allowed just the one run on three hits in 5 2/3 innings. Reliever Wyatt Olds wiggled out of a jam in the sixth after Suarez exited, walking two batters to load the bases, then falling behind pinch hitter Jake Fraley 3-1. Olds came back to strike out Fraley.
The Red Sox faced more trouble in the ninth, with reliever Erik Miller still searching for his command. Closer Aroldis Chapman remains day to day with lat tightness, and Tracy turned to Miller for the ninth with Garrett Whitlock having a heavy load of late.
Miller allowed a run in the ninth on an infield single, a wild pitch, a walk and a groundout. He loaded the bases after a strikeout got away on a wild pitch, but escaped the jam with a groundout to close it out.
Clinching their postseason spot with a week left in the regular season would allow the Red Sox to breathe and reset some players before the postseason. But they’re not there yet. Saturday awaits.
“It just kind of felt like a playoff game,” Anthony said. “Getting into that mode is huge from an at-bat standpoint and from a big-game standpoint of constantly being the next man up.”

Red Sox pitcher Payton Tolle drew all the attention during the team's annual rookie dress-up day after Thursday's series finale against the Rangers. Boston won the tie 4-3, avoiding a series sweep on the road.
While Willson Contreras gave a postgame interview in the clubhouse, Tolle reportedly tried to squeeze into his orange Lorax costume and yelled, "There's going to be ripping." The incident prompted numerous fan reactions.
Here is a picture of Tolle in the Lorax costume, shared on X:
Fans reacted hilariously to the photo. Here are some of them:
"I need video of this more than anything in my life," one fan commented.
"Tolle single-handedly saving baseball this season," another fan commented.
Tolle is having a remarkable rookie season with the Red Sox. He is 9-6 with a 3.02 ERA, 166 strikeouts, and a 1.07 WHIP through 25 starts. The 23-year-old is scheduled to make two more starts for the rest of the season.
The Red Sox opened the crucial three-game intra-divisional series against Tampa Bay with a win on Friday night. Leadoff hitter Roman Anthony was the offensive star, with a couple of hits and three RBIs.
On the mound, Ranger Suarez allowed just one run, walked five, and struck out five over 5.2 IP, as Boston won the game 4-2.
The Red Sox Are All But Certain to Face the Yankees in The AL Wild Card Series
The Yankees are currently second in the AL East, just four games behind the Rays, with the Red Sox at 5.5 games back. The Bombers are projected to secure the fourth seed, and Boston the fifth, in the postseason.
The three-game Wild Card series is scheduled to begin on Sept. 29 at Yankee Stadium, based on the current seedings. The only way the matchups could be altered is if New York overcomes a four-game deficit to Tampa Bay with just nine games left in the regular season.
The Red Sox face the Rays on Saturday in Game 2 at Tropicana Field.

item.content:encoded:
Roman Anthony Powers Red Sox Past Rays, Closer To Playoff Berth originally appeared on NESN. Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Boston Red Sox spent much of Friday night walking a tightrope. Roman Anthony made sure they had enough of a cushion to survive. Anthony homered and drove in three runs, Ranger Suárez battled through 5 2/3 innings and the Red Sox held on for a 4-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field.
Boston improved to 84-70 with its second consecutive victory and snapped Tampa Bay's six-game winning streak. The Red Sox entered the series opener with a magic number of three to clinch an American League wild-card berth and could secure their postseason spot as early as Saturday.
It was not a comfortable victory.
Red Sox pitchers issued nine walks, including four over the final four innings. The Rays loaded the bases in both the sixth and ninth but went 0-for-13 with runners in scoring position and stranded 12 runners. Erik Miller finally ended the ninth-inning adventure by getting Chandler Simpson to ground out with the bases loaded.
Here are three takeaways from Boston's important victory.
Roman Anthony Sets Tone Immediately
Anthony did not wait long to make his presence felt. The Red Sox rookie crushed Ian Seymour's third pitch of the game 438 feet to center field, giving Boston a 1-0 lead before most of the announced crowd of 23,342 had settled into its seats.
It was Anthony's fifth home run of the season and the third leadoff homer of his young career. The Rays answered in the bottom of the first when Junior Caminero drove in Yandy Díaz with a groundout, but Anthony struck again one inning later.
Trevor Story singled and Caleb Durbin followed with another base hit. After Nate Eaton walked to load the bases, Anthony delivered a two-out single to right that scored Story and Durbin. Anthony finished 2-for-5 with three RBIs, accounting for nearly all of Boston's offense on one of the biggest nights of its season.
Jahmai Jones supplied the other run by launching a 414-foot solo homer to left in the third inning. Jones' sixth home run gave Boston a 4-1 advantage that held until the ninth.
Ranger Suárez Bends Without Breaking
Suárez rarely had a clean inning, but the left-hander consistently found his way out of trouble. The Boston starter allowed only three hits and one run while striking out five. He also issued five walks and needed 98 pitches to record 17 outs.
His best defensive moment came in the fourth inning.
Taylor Walls hit a 100-mph line drive directly back at Suárez, who made the catch before throwing to first base to double off Nick Fortes. The play erased a scoring opportunity and helped Suárez navigate another stressful inning. The left-hander improved to 8-4 and lowered his ERA to 3.27.
Wyatt Olds entered with two outs in the sixth and immediately made matters worse by issuing two walks. He recovered to strike out Jake Fraley with the bases loaded, preserving Boston's three-run advantage.
Greg Weissert provided the calmest portion of the night, allowing one hit over two scoreless innings.
Erik Miller Survives Chaotic Ninth Inning
The Red Sox carried a 4-1 lead into the ninth, but Miller turned the final three outs into a full-blown ordeal. The left-hander issued two walks and threw three wild pitches during a 32-pitch inning. Jonathan Aranda drove in one run with a fielder's choice, cutting Boston's lead to 4-2.
Tampa Bay eventually loaded the bases with two outs, bringing Simpson to the plate as the potential winning run. Miller induced a ground ball to third baseman Durbin, who completed the force play at second to end the game. Miller earned his fifth save despite allowing one run, one hit and two walks.
Boston will take the victory, especially at this stage of the season, but the nine walks gave the club another issue to clean up before October. The Red Sox will attempt to clinch their postseason berth Saturday when they continue the three-game series in Tampa Bay. The Rays are scheduled to start right-hander Freddy Peralta, while Boston has yet to announce it's starter.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Roman Anthony homered and drove in three runs and the Boston Red Sox took a big step toward clinching an American League playoff spot with a 4-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday night.
The Red Sox, who entered Friday with a magic number of three, could secure a wild-card spot as early as Saturday.
Junior Caminero and Jonathan Aranda drove in runs for the post-season-bound Rays. They had won six in a row.
Anthony hit the game’s third pitch from Ian Seymour (9-7) into the right-field seats for his third career leadoff homer. Then, in the second inning, Anthony broke a 1-1 tie and drove in two more runs with a two-out single.
Jahmai Jones gave Boston a 4-1 advantage with his own solo homer to lead off the third. Caleb Durbin added two hits for the Red Sox, who own the American League’s third-best record (84-70), behind the Rays and Yankees.
Red Sox starter Ranger Suarez (8-4) threw 5 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and one run with five walks and five strikeouts. He also snared Taylor Walls’ 100-mph liner in the fourth, before completing an inning-ending double play.
Tampa Bay couldn’t capitalize on multiple opportunities, including nine Red Sox walks. The Rays left the bases loaded in the sixth and ninth, when Erik Miller retired Chandler Simpson on a game-ending grounder. Tampa Bay was 0 for 13 with runners in scoring position.
Boston left-hander Erik Miller had his fifth save despite a shaky ninth inning, including three wild pitches and two walks.
Up next
Tampa Bay RHP Freddy Peralta (9-11, 4.67 ERA) was set to start Saturday. Boston had yet to announce a starter.

item.content:encoded:
Roman Anthony homered and had three RBIs, Jahmai Jones went deep and the Boston Red Sox cooled off the first-place Tampa Bay Rays with a 4-2 victory on Friday night in St. Petersburg, Fla.
The Red Sox (84-70) opened their final road series of the regular season by scoring all of their runs in the first three innings to win for the second consecutive night.
Anthony went 2-for-5, while Caleb Durbin was 2-for-3 as the team produced nine hits.
Starting pitcher Ranger Suarez (8-4) fought control issues but went 5 2/3 innings in earning the win. He allowed one run on three hits while striking out five and walking five.
Junior Caminero doubled, walked twice and drove in a run for Tampa Bay (93-60), but the American League’s top club had only five hits, was a brutal 0-for-13 with runners in scoring position and had its six-game winning streak snapped.
Starter Ian Seymour (9-7) was hit hard in the first two innings and finished by allowing four runs on seven hits in five frames. He whiffed five and walked two.
On the third pitch of the game, leadoff hitter Anthony crushed a Statcast-estimated 438-foot blast to center field. It was the left fielder’s fifth homer.
Caminero’s RBI groundout tied it in the bottom half, but Anthony did more damage by ripping a two-out single to right for a 3-1 lead in the second.
Jones made it 4-1 leading off the third by lining Seymour’s changeup out to left for his sixth homer.
Suarez got out of a slight jam in the third after Caminero walked and Ryan Vilade singled, but he retired red-hot Chandler Simpson and Jonny DeLuca to maintain the three-run lead.
The home club put together a strong threat in the sixth after Wyatt Olds relieved Suarez and issued two walks to fill the bases with two outs. However, he battled back in the count against pinch hitter Jake Fraley and struck him out.
In the ninth, Jonathan Aranda’s groundout scored a run, but Erik Miller got Simpson to ground out to second with the bases loaded for his fifth save.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG -- Roman Anthony atacó el tercer pitcheo del juego de la noche del viernes en el Tropicana Field, quizás dejando claro, con un batazo de 438 pies según la proyección de Statcast hacia la corta distancia del jardín derecho-central, que su mala racha ha terminado.
Por si fuera poco, el joven de 22 años volvió al plato un inning después y conectó el primer hit de su carrera en 11 visitas al plato con las bases llenas, un sencillo de dos carreras hacia el jardín derecho.
Anthony fue quien encabezó la ofensiva mientras los Medias Rojas (84-70) se acercaron más a asegurar su boleto a la postemporada con una victoria por 4-2 sobre los Rays, quienes tienen el mejor récord de la Liga Americana con 93-60 y llegaron al encuentro con una racha de seis triunfos consecutivos.
Aunque Anthony estuvo encendido con el bate en sus primeros cuatro juegos tras regresar de la lista de lesionados, sus siguientes 12 encuentros antes del viernes fueron muy distintos: línea ofensiva de .137/.214/.296, con un extrabase en 56 visitas al plato.
Desde la lomita, Ranger Suárez (8-4, EFE de 3.27) completó su tercera apertura sólida consecutiva, pese a otorgar cinco bases por bolas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. El zurdo logró salir de los problemas que él mismo generó, permitiendo apenas tres hits y una carrera, con cinco ponches en 5.2 innings y 98 pitcheos, 56 de ellos strikes.
Wyatt Olds, quien últimamente ha pasado de ser un llamado sin muchos reflectores a una pieza importante del bullpen, otorgó bases por bolas a los primeros dos bateadores que enfrentó al entrar en lugar de Suárez, pero salió del apuro al ponchar al bateador emergente Jake Fraley.
Greg Weissert respondió con dos innings importantes, en los que sorteó un hit.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG – Roman Anthony tore into the third pitch of Friday night’s game at Tropicana Field, perhaps making a Statcast-projected 438-foot statement into a short porch in right-center field that his slump is over.
For good measure, the 22-year-old stepped up an inning later and came up with his first career hit in 11 plate appearances with the bases loaded, bashing a two-run single to right.
It was Anthony leading the offense as the Sox (84-70) pushed closer to punching their ticket to the postseason with a 4-2 victory over the Rays, who have an American League-best 93-60 record and came into this one with a six-game winning streak.
While Anthony swung a hot bat in his first four games back from the injured list, his next 12 games entering Friday went like this: a slash line of .137/.214/.296 with one extra-base hit in 56 plate appearances.
From the mound, Ranger Suarez (8-4, 3.27 ERA) turned in his third consecutive solid start, despite issuing a career-high five walks. The lefty worked around the trouble he created, allowing just three hits and one run while striking out five over 5 2/3 innings and 98 pitches (56 strikes).
Wyatt Olds, who has gone from an unheralded callup to a key bullpen piece of late, walked the first two batters he faced when he came on for Suarez, but he escaped by striking out pinch-hitter Jake Fraley.
Greg Weissert came through with two big innings, working around one hit.

item.title: [The Boston Globe] Roman Anthony provides pop as Red Sox hold off first-place Rays - The Boston Globe

item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Tampa Bay Rays have been the best team in the American League for much of this season, particularly at Tropicana Field. But with one All-Star on the injured list and two others unavailable, the Red Sox came away with a 4-2 victory before a crowd of 23,342 as Roman Anthony drove in three runs. item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Tampa Bay Rays have been the best team in the American League for much of this season, particularly at Tropicana Field.
But with one All-Star on the injured list and two others unavailable, the Red Sox came away with a 4-2 victory before a crowd of 23,342 as Roman Anthony drove in three runs.
Now the magic number to clinch a playoff spot is down to two.
Ranger Suarez (8-4) and three relievers walked nine but held the Rays to five hits. Tampa Bay was hitless in 13 at-bats with runners in scoring position and left 12 men on base.
It was an impressive victory for the Sox, considering the 93-60 Rays are close to clinching the best record in the league and home-field advantage through, at least, the American League Championship Series.
The Sox were without Ceddanne Rafaela, who isn’t expected to come off the injured list until next week. Aroldis Chapman (lat strain) and Willson Contreras (bruised right hand) were not available.
With Garrett Whitlock left in the bullpen after pitching Thursday night, the Sox used lefthander Erik Miller to get the final three outs for his first save with the team.
Miller walked two and threw three wild pitches in a wild ninth inning, giving up a run before finally getting Chandler Simpson to ground to second for the final out.
Miller had allowed five runs over 5⅓ innings and put 10 men on base in his previous six appearances.
The Sox didn’t arrive at the team hotel until close to 5 a.m. after beating the Rangers in Texas on Thursday night. The Rays had a day game at home that ended 13 hours earlier. But the Sox had more energy early on.
Anthony blasted the third pitch of the game from Ian Seymour 438 feet to center field for his fifth home run.
Trevor Story and Caleb Durbin led off the second inning with singles. Isiah Kiner-Falefa dropped a bunt to advance the runners before Nate Eaton worked a walk to load the bases.
After Connor Wong struck out, Anthony worked the count full and lined a hard single to right field to drive in two more runs. The three RBIs matched his career high.
Jahmai Jones homered leading off the third inning, a 414-foot shot to left field.
Suarez did not handle the run support very well. He walked a hitter in each of the first four innings and threw 69 pitches. But the Rays scored only one run.
Yandy Diaz walked leading off the bottom of the first, advanced to third on a double by Jonathan Aranda, and scored on Junior Caminero’s groundout.
Suarez was done after 5⅔ innings and 98 pitches, leaving the game with a runner at second. Wyatt Olds walked Liam Hicks and Victor Mesa Jr. on 12 pitches to load the bases.
He fell behind Jake Fraley 3 and 1, then came back to strike him out swinging through a fastball at the top of the strike zone. Olds threw up his hands after finally ending the inning. It wasn’t an elegant outing, but it was ultimately an effective one.
Greg Weissert worked around a two-out double by Caminero in the seventh inning to keep the lead at three runs, then came back for a 1-2-3 eighth.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

item.title: [Boston Herald] Roman Anthony’s big game puts Red Sox on precipice of clinching playoff bid
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: Back in late June when the Red Sox sunk to their lowest depths, the idea that the club might still have a shot at reaching the postseason would have seemed hopelessly optimistic. Yet, here they are with a little over a week left to play in the regular season, and the Red Sox have all but punched their ticket to the playoffs. With their 4-2 win over the Tampa Bay Rays in Friday’s series opener, the Red Sox can now clinch a playoff spot as soon as Saturday. The club’s magic number, which stood at
item.content:encoded:
Back in late June when the Red Sox sunk to their lowest depths, the idea that the club might still have a shot at reaching the postseason would have seemed hopelessly optimistic.
Yet, here they are with a little over a week left to play in the regular season, and the Red Sox have all but punched their ticket to the playoffs.
With their 4-2 win over the Tampa Bay Rays in Friday’s series opener, the Red Sox can now clinch a playoff spot as soon as Saturday. The club’s magic number, which stood at three entering the night, will drop to either one or two depending on the outcome of Friday’s late game between the Rangers and Blue Jays.
A Rangers win would mean the Red Sox could clinch with a win on Saturday, while a Blue Jays win would necessitate a win and a Blue Jays loss.
Following a string of poor offensive performances, Friday got off to a much stronger start at the plate. Roman Anthony put the Red Sox in front with a solo home run to lead off the game, and after the Rays tied it up in the bottom half of the first, Anthony delivered again in the second with a go-ahead two-run single with the bases loaded off Rays starter Ian Seymour, an alumnus of St. John’s High School in Shrewsbury.
Anthony finished 2 for 4 with three RBI, and the Red Sox never looked back.
“Taking that first one is big,” Anthony told NESN’s Jahmai Webster postgame. “Any win you can get against a team like that it’s a great win, so it’s a great day.”
Anthony’s first-inning blast was smoked. Measured at 107.7 mph off the bat and traveling 438 feet, the solo home run to right field narrowly missed landing in Tropicana Field’s ray tank.
His two-run single in the second inning was hit even harder, coming off the bat at 108.7 mph. Anthony came through after Trevor Story and Caleb Durbin led off the inning with singles, Isiah Kiner-Falefa moved them into scoring position with a sacrifice bunt and Nate Eaton walked to load the bases.
It was doubly encouraging given Anthony’s recent struggles at the plate. After a hot start coming off the injured list, the outfielder came into Friday batting just .137 with one extra base hit over his past 12 games.
“I’ve been grinding, but that’s the beauty of this team,” Anthony said. “You’re never down and you’re never out.”
Jahmai Jones capped off the early offense with a solo shot to lead off the top of the third.
Tampa Bay scored its early run in the first after Yandy Diaz drew a leadoff walk, advanced to third on a Jonathan Aranda double and scored on a Junior Caminero groundout. But that was all the damage the Rays could do against Ranger Suarez, who allowed one run over 5 2/3 innings while falling one out short of his third consecutive quality start.
Suarez was uncharacteristically wild, walking five batters, but he limited the damage by allowing just three hits while striking out five.
The walks almost cost the Red Sox in the sixth inning.
Still leading by three, Suarez issued his fifth and final walk to lead off the sixth before recording two quick outs to finish his outing. But Wyatt Olds came on and immediately walked the first two men he faced, loading the bases and bringing the go-ahead run to the plate.
A brief mound visit followed, and Olds dug deep and struck out pinch hitter Jake Fraley to escape the inning unscathed.
“It was a weird game all the way around, we walked nine in total, Ranger walked five but still almost completed six innings and he was very competitive with men on base,” Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters in St. Petersburg. “He lost some counts and behind more counts today, but he was able to make really good pitches with people on base.”
Walks put the Red Sox in one more jam in the bottom of the ninth inning.
With Aroldis Chapman unavailable with a lat issue and Garrett Whitlock having pitched on Thursday, Erik Miller took the mound in the ninth and walked three men. He allowed a run to score on a Victor Mesa Jr. groundout, and the third walk to Caminero brought the winning run to the plate with two outs.
Miller struck out Ryan Vilade, but the ball got away from Connor Wong and the Rays batter reached safely to extend the game and load the bases. But Miller fought back and drew a game-ending groundout from Chandler Simpson, leaving the Rays 0 for 13 with runners in scoring position and 12 men left on base in spite of the nine walks issued by the Red Sox pitching staff.
While Miller has now walked seven batters over his last 3 1/3 innings, Tracy said he felt the left-hander looked much better on Friday despite all of the traffic.
“I thought he was way more competitive,” Tracy said. “Everything was around the zone, stuff was good, he was getting some swing and miss like he usually does so I take a lot of good out of that outing.”
The win marked Boston’s first at Tropicana Field this season, and the club hopes plenty more will follow in the days and weeks to come. The Rays have long been in the driver’s seat for the AL East title, and barring a complete collapse over the final week Tampa Bay should soon lock down the American League’s top seed and a bye to the divisional round.
That means if the Red Sox (84-70) can get past the Yankees in the AL Wild Card Series, they’d be headed right back to St. Petersburg to face the Rays in a rematch of the 2021 ALDS.
But first, the Red Sox hope to pop some bottles in the Tropicana Field visitor’s clubhouse before they fly back to Boston. First pitch on Saturday is scheduled for 4:10 p.m.

item.content:encoded:
Red Sox Insert Jahmai Jones into Lineup Against Rays Lefty
The Boston Red Sox placed designated hitter Jahmai Jones in the third spot in the starting lineup on Friday against Tampa Bay Rays left-hander Ian Seymour at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.
According to MLB.com, Jones sits in the heart of the order between outfielders Roman Anthony and Wilyer Abreu. Shortstop Trevor Story and first baseman Nick Sogard also feature in the top five positions for Boston.
Left-hander Ranger Suárez gets the start on the mound for Boston against Tampa Bay's Seymour. Seymour enters the contest holding a 9-6 record with a 4.27 ERA and 150 strikeouts on the season, according to official team statistics.
Boston manager Chad Tracy opted to stack the right-handed hitting Jones near the top of the batting order due to ongoing injuries and lack of availability among several key players, including Ceddanne Rafaela, Masataka Yoshida, Curtis Mead, and Willson Contreras.
According to MLB Trade Rumors, Boston acquired Jones off waivers on July 14 after the Detroit Tigers designated him for assignment, sending pitching prospect Jojo Ingrassia to Detroit as compensation.
Jones struggled with Detroit this season, batting .137 with a .221 slugging percentage across 105 plate appearances before his release. However, he has turned his season around in Boston, slashing .362/.464/.681 with three home runs and eight RBIs in 56 plate appearances.
Friday marks the 20th time overall this season that Jones has occupied the third spot in a starting lineup, having done so 19 times prior across his stints with Detroit and Boston. In those previous 35 plate appearances in the third spot, he posted a .219 batting average and a .661 OPS.
According to FanGraphs, the platoon splits support Boston's heavy usage of Jones against left-handed pitching. Across 138 plate appearances against lefties this year, Jones has recorded a .223 batting average, a .333 on-base percentage, and a .420 slugging percentage with five home runs, 15 walks, and 14 RBIs.
Conversely, Jones has registered just a .130 average in 23 at-bats against right-handed pitchers, with all five of his home runs this season coming exclusively against left-handers. He previously hit a two-run home run off Seymour during a July 18 matchup at Fenway Park.
Boston enters the three-game series against the American League East-leading Rays with an 83-70 record, holding the second AL Wild Card position and a five-game lead over the Cleveland Guardians. NESN reports Boston's magic number to clinch a postseason berth stands at three with nine games remaining on their schedule.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Willson Contreras' frustrations following hit by pitch are a brewing Red Sox problem
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: Willson Contreras played a key role in the Boston Red Sox's come-from-behind win in the series finale against the Texas Rangers, but not in a way he would have preferred. Contreras was plunked in the hand by struggling Rangers reliever Jakob Junis in the top of the eighth, setting the scene for Trevor Story to launch a go-ahead three-run homer off All-Star closer Jacob Latz. The good news is that Contreras underwent x-rays following the game, and they came back clean. The veteran didn't seem to
item.content:encoded:
Willson Contreras played a key role in the Boston Red Sox's come-from-behind win in the series finale against the Texas Rangers, but not in a way he would have preferred. Contreras was plunked in the hand by struggling Rangers reliever Jakob Junis in the top of the eighth, setting the scene for Trevor Story to launch a go-ahead three-run homer off All-Star closer Jacob Latz.
The good news is that Contreras underwent x-rays following the game, and they came back clean. The veteran didn't seem to agree with the diagnosis, saying that it felt like a fracture and that he's fractured that hand before and experienced some numbness. More importantly, he's frustrated.
“If nobody does anything about it, I’m going to keep getting hit. That’s the way I see it. That’s it,” Contreras said, via Tim Healey of The Boston Globe.
Contreras has been hit by a pitch 24 times this season, third-most in the league. Of course, he also crowds the plate more than almost any hitter in the game. You want to claim the entire plate as your own; expect opposing pitchers to try and prove to you that the inside corner is, in fact, theirs.
By the sound of it, that is lost on Contreras. It seems as if the former St. Louis Cardinal wants one of Boston's pitchers to go out and start beaning batters in retaliation. That might be how things were done in the olden days, but now that's a recipe for escalation, a potential brawl, and possible suspensions.
Given that he doesn't feel as if any of the hurlers have come to his defense, it's likely that won't change. These bad feelings could become a cause for concern, and even more so with us approaching October's doorstep.
Willson Contreras could be threatening Red Sox chemistry again with latest HBP outrage
On the field, Contreras has had a fantastic first season in Boston. His 27 homers are already a career high, and if it holds, his .387 on-base percentage will be a career-best, too. Meanwhile, his .518 slugging percentage is the second-best mark of his career. There was a reason why he was voted a top AL MVP contender in an MLB.com poll at the end of August.
That's been great, but there have been issues. Contreras made some confusing comments after Alex Cora was dismissed, seemingly taking a shot at the team's young players in the process. He has also gotten into it with fans after being booed for not running out a ground ball back in August, further cementing his reputation as a prickly player.
At the same time, before the tide turned on the Red Sox's season and trade rumors enveloped him, he stated that he wouldn't waive his no-trade clause, desiring to finish his career in Boston.
Overall, it's odd. At times, it has seemed as if he doesn't really want to be here, despite his protest that, in fact, Boston is the only place he envisions himself playing.
This latest incident is more dangerous. Who knows what is said behind closed doors, but hurt bodies and hurt feelings don't go well together. If Contreras pushes the "defense" issue, it could cause a real rift. The pitchers could side with each other, while the hitters rally around Contreras.
The lines could also be different if there are enough players on either side of the positional divide with a more updated view of bean ball, so that different cliques could form.
The Red Sox have bigger issues at hand right now. They're going to have to figure out their postseason roster crunch. They're hoping that Aroldis Chapman's sore lat isn't anything serious. They need to find a way to get Roman Anthony's bat going before the playoffs begin. What they don't have time for is Contreras getting in his feelings because he got hit while standing on top of the plate.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox secured a major 4-3 victory over the Texas Rangers on Thursday night in their series finale, avoiding the sweep.
On Friday, they’ll start a weekend series against the American League-best Tampa Bay Rays, and ahead of the opener, Red Sox manager Chad Tracy made a notable lineup decision involving All-Star Willson Contreras after a pitch hit him on the hand Thursday.
Red Sox Announce Contreras Decision
X-rays came back negative after Thursday’s game on Contreras’ hand, fortunately. However, he is not in the starting lineup for the opener against Tampa Bay.
Starting at first base in place of Contreras will be Nick Sogard, who will bat second in the order behind leadoff hitter Roman Anthony.
Stepping into the three and four holes will be designated hitter Jahmai Jones and outfielder Wilyer Abreu.
Here’s the full Red Sox lineup:

Contreras’ 2026 Season
In his first year with the Red Sox, Contreras has appeared in 129 games and recorded 68 runs, 123 hits, 27 home runs, and 81 RBIs across 446 at-bats while batting .276 with a .518 slugging percentage and a .905 OPS.
Looking at the Red Sox
Boston enters Friday night with an 83-70 overall record and sits on the verge of clinching a postseason bid. If they clinch, they’ll enter the playoffs as the second Wild Card team.
If the current standings hold, the Red Sox would travel to the Bronx to face the New York Yankees in a best-of-three Wild Card series.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Trevor Story's game-winning home run vs. Rangers is a reminder of his under-the-radar Red Sox role
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: The Boston Red Sox seem to be stalling out at the worst possible time. The offense has had trouble limiting strikeouts, advancing runners and hitting, in general with a clinching opportunity on the line. But under the doom and gloom of the rest of the offense, there is hidden a triumphant return from injury by an unexpected player: Trevor Story. He played hero on September 17 against the Texas Rangers with an eighth-inning, three-run homer to stave off a sweep and help his team inch closer to cl
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox seem to be stalling out at the worst possible time. The offense has had trouble limiting strikeouts, advancing runners and hitting, in general with a clinching opportunity on the line.
But under the doom and gloom of the rest of the offense, there is hidden a triumphant return from injury by an unexpected player: Trevor Story. He played hero on September 17 against the Texas Rangers with an eighth-inning, three-run homer to stave off a sweep and help his team inch closer to clinching a playoff berth.
Even before that, Story had been hitting well while the rest of Boston's bats have faltered, including some of its best, like Willson Contreras and Roman Anthony (subscription required). Story is slashing .349/.359/.508 with seven doubles, a home run and nine RBI since he returned from the injured list on August 30. Boston's lineup hasn't been long enough lately to make the best of its minimal offensive production, so Story's efforts have gone under-the-radar.
There's quite a bit of swing and miss in Story's game, as there always has been. He's fanned at a 31.3 percent clip in the 16 games he's played since coming off the IL, which hasn't helped Boston's strikeout totals each game. But Story got the job done when the Sox needed him most, and for that he deserves credit.
Trevor Story has been a bright spot in Red Sox's offense throughout September slump
The Red Sox have looked utterly lifeless at the plate and Story was able to break through the ugly spell. With any luck, his game-saver from Thursday night will inspire his teammates to free themselves from whatever late-season funk they're in, which has delayed their clinching ceremony enough already.
It's reassuring to see Story get hot with just a few series remaining. He also performed exceptionally well last September with a .302/.337/.458 slash line, six doubles, three home runs and 12 RBI over 22 games that month. He's looking like a weapon en-route to a Wild Card matchup for the second year in a row.
Story has also seemingly crushed the slump he was in when the season started. The shortstop batted only .206/.244/.303 with 57 strikeouts to just eight walks over 41 games before his injury. Before Story and the Red Sox revealed the sports hernia bugging the infielder, fans were under the impression that another rough year was coming, but pain from the injury might've severely hampered his play.
After Boston went without signing a true slugger over the offseason (a Pete Alonso or Kyle Schwarber type, a more consistent home run hitter than Contreras), it needed Story to build off his 2025 season for the offense to be at its best. There hasn't been much power in Story's game yet, but maybe his game-saving homer against the Rangers changes the tides. Story has been one of few bright spots this month in the Red Sox's underachieving offense and the rest of the team needs to play closer to his level to maintain its Wild Card standing as the regular season draws to a close.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Boston Red Sox Shortstop Trevor Story Has Blunt Quote After Win Over Texas Rangers
item.dc:creator: Scott Roche
item.description: When the Boston Red Sox lost shortstop Trevor Story to an injury earlier this year, one big question was how they were going to replace him. Interim manager Chad Tracy used a couple of different players who more than held things down until the veteran was going to return. When Story was eligible to return, Andruw Monasterio found himself as the odd man out at shortstop. However, Story had to prove that he was healthy enough to hold down the job late in the season. As it turns out, he is. After c
item.content:encoded:
When the Boston Red Sox lost shortstop Trevor Story to an injury earlier this year, one big question was how they were going to replace him. Interim manager Chad Tracy used a couple of different players who more than held things down until the veteran was going to return.
When Story was eligible to return, Andruw Monasterio found himself as the odd man out at shortstop. However, Story had to prove that he was healthy enough to hold down the job late in the season.
As it turns out, he is. After coming up clutch on Thursday night, Story didn't mince words about the noise that there is outside the locker room about him.
Boston Red Sox Shortstop Trevor Story Drops Honest Quote on Outside Noise
Trailing 3-0 against the Texas Rangers on Thursday night in Arlington, Boston was staring at being swept as the game moved into the late innings. After they plated a run in the top of the seventh on a Roman Anthony fielder's choice.
In the top of the eighth, Story stepped up to the plate with two runners on and one out. Story crushed a curveball from Texas' Jacob Latz for a three-run home run and 4-3 lead. The Red Sox got the final six outs to secure a one-run win. After the game, Story didn't mince words about the outside noise and hearing it.
"I'm not really motivated by outside noise, but you hear it," said Story, per Alex Speier of the Boston Globe. "I try to use it in the way that fits me best. The point of getting the surgery was to come back and try to be the player that I know I can be, and it's starting to show."
Halfway through the month of September, Story is slashing .327/.339/.473 in September with one home run and six RBIs.
"He's been great," Tracy said, per Perla Paredes of MLB.com. "He's got a hit in every game but one. That was a hell of an at-bat against a really good pitcher in a really big spot and a huge swing. Obviously needed a win, but all the credit to him.
"You're one pitch away in a spot like that, where he can change a game, like we saw it numerous times in the second half of last year. So, like I said, it was a massive swing."
Trevor Story Looking To Find Swing Before Playoffs
There are nine games for the Red Sox before the playoffs begin. Boston is likely headed for an American League wild-card series against the New York Yankees. The series for the second straight year will be in the Bronx.
Boston has a three-game series against the first-place Tampa Bay Rays this weekend in Central Florida. They then close out the season with a pair of three-game series at home against the Cleveland Guardians and Chicago Cubs.
Finishing the regular season strong will be key. Boston has struggled in September and is limping into the playoffs. A healthy Story could be key for Boston come postseason baseball.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Boston Red Sox Shortstop Trevor Story Has Blunt Quote After Win Over Texas Rangers appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] Sudden Aroldis Chapman injury issue adds uncertain wrinkle to Yankees-Red Sox showdown
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox seem destined for another October clash. You can smell the narrative building now. The Red Sox will be painted as the underdogs due to their horrid start to the season. Fine. Whatever makes them feel better. For the Yankees, this could be a tipping point, a chance to regain that sense of dominance over their hated rival. To that end, New York might have just gotten a piece of news that could further tip the scales in its favor, and it has to do old "friend
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox seem destined for another October clash. You can smell the narrative building now. The Red Sox will be painted as the underdogs due to their horrid start to the season. Fine. Whatever makes them feel better.
For the Yankees, this could be a tipping point, a chance to regain that sense of dominance over their hated rival. To that end, New York might have just gotten a piece of news that could further tip the scales in its favor, and it has to do old "friend" Aroldis Chapman.
After dropping the first two games of their series against the Texas Rangers, Boston mounted a late-inning comeback following a Trevor Story three-run homer in the eighth inning against Texas's all-world closer Jacob Latz. Coming out to secure the victory in the ninth wasn't Chapman, though; instead, it was another former Yankee, Garrett Whitlock. After the game, it was revealed that Chapman was "unavailable" because he's dealing with a sore lat.
Red Sox interim manager said that it's an issue that Chapman has been dealing with for a few days, and that the team will be conservative with his usage for the time being. The 38-year-old, who recently learned the importance of throwing strikes, has seen his command get spotty over his last two outings, issuing three walks in the process. Perhaps the injury is to blame?
Red Sox injury issues, including Aroldis Chapman, Willson Contreras, and others, could give Yankees the upper hand
At this point, it's unclear whether or not Chapman will need to head to the IL, but either way him being less than 100% bodes well for the Yankees. That will be especially true if he remains active and reverts to his wild ways in the upcoming playoff matchup.
Chapman isn't the only Boston player banged up, either. Willson Contreras was hit by a pitch on the hand during the Red Sox's win over the Rangers. X-rays were initially negative, but the former St. Louis Cardinal said he's suffered hand fractures before and that this felt the same way. He'll be sent for imaging and further tests to determine the true extent.
Contreras has been hit a total of 24 times this season, the third-most in baseball. He seems frustrated, too, saying that it will keep happening "if nobody does anything about it." Sounds like he's frustrated that Boston pitchers haven't come to his defense, threatening to cause an issue for the Red Sox even if his hand injury proves to be nothing serious.
That's not the end of the problems for the Red Sox. Roman Anthony, who missed nearly four months due to a torn finger ligament, is slumping hard. After an initial burst in his first two games back after being activated on August 30, Anthony has slashed just .200/.268/.338 thus far in September.
The biggest news of all, though, is Chapman. If he avoids the IL but is diminished, it could give the Yankees a key advantage in the most crucial moments of the expected matchup. The Sox's other primary bullpen lefty, Erik Miller, is also suffering from mechanical issues at a particularly brutal time. Capitalizing on that edge will be a must, and if the Red Sox fall to New York due to a Chapman postseason meltdown, the moment will be that much sweeter.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Red Sox salvage finale in Texas thanks to Trevor Story's 3-run homer

Josh Jung hit a solo home run for Texas (76-77), which fell a game behind the Houston Astros (77-76) at the top of
item.content:encoded:
Trevor Story hit a three-run homer in the eighth inning as the Boston Red Sox overcame a three-run deficit to defeat the Texas Rangers 4-3 on Thursday in Arlington, Texas.
Story’s blast came against Texas closer Jacob Latz (3-3) and erased a 3-1 deficit.
The victory allowed Boston (83-70) to avoid being swept in the three-game series and ended the Rangers’ four-game winning streak. Josh Jung hit a solo home run for Texas (76-77), which fell a game behind the Houston Astros (77-76) at the top of the American League West.
Wyatt Olds (2-0) earned the win by tossing one scoreless inning. Boston starter Sonny Gray allowed three runs on three hits in 6 1/3 innings. He struck out six and walked three.
Texas had the tying run on first with one out in the ninth, but Garrett Whitlock got Jake Burger to ground into a game-ending double play for his fourth save.
Danny Jansen had two of the Rangers’ four hits, including an RBI single.
Boston’s Willson Contreras left the game after he was hit by a pitch on his right hand in the eighth inning. Contreras leads the Red Sox with 27 home runs.
Jung hit a solo shot in the first inning to open the scoring. It was his 10th homer of the season.
Texas extended its lead to 3-0 in the third. After two walks and a sacrifice bunt, Jansen singled home Wyatt Langford, and Burger scored on Evan Carter’s sacrifice bunt.
The Red Sox got on the scoreboard in the seventh. Nate Eaton and Caleb Durbin walked, and Eaton took third on a flyout. A throwing error by second baseman Nicky Lopez on Roman Anthony’s grounder brought in Eaton.
In the eighth, Boston’s Wilyer Abreu walked and Contreras was hit by a Jakob Junis pitch. Latz entered and got Adley Rutschman to foul out before Story belted a 2-2 curveball to left-center, handing Boston a 4-3 lead. It was Story’s fourth homer of the year.
The Boston offense struggled in the first two games of the series. The Red Sox struck out 15 times as the Rangers won 4-2 on Tuesday, and the visitors were held to three hits in a 7-3 loss on Wednesday.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Story reaparece con jonrón y completa remontada de los Medias Rojas
This browser does not support the video element.
ARLINGTON -- Trevor Story esperó más de cuatro meses para conectar su siguiente jonrón. Y llegó justo a tiempo para los Medias Rojas.
Story finalmente despertó con un cuadrangular de tres carreras que puso a Boston al frente en el octavo inning la noche del jueves, impulsando a los Medias Rojas a una victoria por 4-3 sobre los Rangers en el Globe Life Field y ayudándolos a evitar su primera barrida desde julio.
Wilyer Abreu abrió el octavo episodio con una base por bolas antes de que Willson Contreras fuera golpeado por un lanzamiento y saliera del juego, con Isiah Kiner-Falefa ingresando como corredor emergente. Story entonces atacó una curva de 80.3 mph y la mandó en línea entre los jardines izquierdo y central para su primer vuelacercas desde el 13 de mayo y su cuarto de la temporada.
Boston había comenzado a reducir la desventaja un capítulo antes. Después de boletos consecutivos a Caleb Durbin y Nate Eaton, Roman Anthony bateó un rodado para una jugada forzada que permitió anotar a Eaton. Un error en tiro del segunda base Nicky López en la jugada permitió que Anthony avanzara a la intermedia.
La remontada en las últimas entradas llegó después de que Sonny Gray mantuviera a los Medias Rojas a una distancia alcanzable pese a un complicado comienzo de su apertura.
El derecho de 36 años lanzó 6.1 entradas, permitiendo tres carreras y tres hits, con seis ponches y tres bases por bolas en 102 pitcheos, su mayor cantidad de la temporada, de los cuales 67 fueron strikes.

item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas (AP) — Trevor Story hit a three-run home run off All-Star closer Jacob Latz in the eighth inning, capping a comeback from a three-run deficit as the Boston Red Sox beat Texas 4-3 on Thursday night and dropped the Rangers out of the AL West lead.
Texas (76-77) had won four straight games to gain a share of the lead but dropped one game behind Houston (77-76), which holds the tiebreaker. The Rangers trail by two games for the last AL wild card.
Boston (83-70) has a five-game lead for the top AL wild card and improved to 8-59 when trailing after seven innings. Texas dropped to 63-2 when leading after seven innings.
Latz (3-3) entered after Wilyer Abreu walked starting the eighth and Willson Contreras was hit by a pitch from Jakob Junis.
Latz struck out Adley Rutschman and Story, who is from nearby Irving, reached down for Latz's second straight low curveball and drove the ball over the left-field wall for his fourth home run this season.
Boston’s Wyatt Olds (2-0) got three outs and Garrett Whitlock pitched the ninth for his fourth save in eight chances, getting Jake Burger to ground into a game-ending double play.
Josh Jung hit a first-inning homer off Sonny Gray, and Texas opened a 3-0 lead in the second on Danny Jansen's RBI single and Evan Carter's safety squeeze bunt.
Roman Anthony hit into a run-scoring forceout in the seventh.
Texas’ Cody Bradford followed a one-inning opener with 4 1/3 shutout innings, seeking his first major league since Sept. 18, 2024. He missed last season following elbow surgery.
Gray gave up three hits in 6 1/3 innings, throwing a season-high 102 pitches.
Up Next
Red Sox: LHP Ranger Suarez (7-4, 3.33) will go against LHP Ian Seymour (9-6, 4.27) on Friday at Tampa Bay.
Rangers: RHP Kumar Rocker (5-11, 4.54) starts Friday against visiting Toronto and RHP Dylan Cease (11-5, 2.38).
